literature.headline_zh: 季节性流感病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期季节性流感病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 结果表明,流感 发病率 降低了实验室确诊流感的 发病率 以及与流感疾病相关的并发症的风险。 [10.58347/tml.2026.1767c]
2017 年和 2018 年分离的病毒的 PB1 和 PB2 片段属于 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 谱系的不同簇,表明可能存在额外的重配事件。猪分离株形成一个离散簇,与 2007-2024 年注册的人类季节性 甲型H3N2流感病毒 菌株相距 ≥ 4 个抗原单位。 [10.1007/s00705-026-06779-y]
该研究证明了使用数字 PCR 检测和区分废水样品中的禽类病毒和 季节性流感 病毒的可行性。 [10.3201/eid3211.261234]
ADAR 相关的 突变 显示与病毒载量 (p < 0.0001) 和年龄 (p = 0.0051) 呈显着负相关,尤其是在 75 岁以上的患者中。ADAR 相关 突变 与病毒载量之间的关联与年龄、炎症和疾病严重程度无关 (p < 0.001)。 [10.1080/23744235.2026.2753489]
优化的 NA mRNA 疫苗,特别是 F1 和 F2,提供了针对 H3N2 攻击的完全保护,减少了肺部的病毒复制,并诱导可检测到的针对异源 H3N2 病毒的神经氨酸酶抑制 (NAI) 活性。 [10.71150/jm.2609004]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The results indicated that influenza vaccination reduces the incidence of laboratory-confirmed influenza and the risk of complications associated with influenza illness. [10.58347/tml.2026.1767c]

The PB1 and PB2 segments of the viruses isolated in 2017 and 2018 belonged to different clusters of the A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage, suggesting a possible additional reassortment event. The swine isolates formed a discrete cluster ≥ 4 antigenic units distant from human seasonal A(H3N2) strains registered in 2007-2024. [10.1007/s00705-026-06779-y]
The study demonstrated the feasibility of using digital PCR to detect and differentiate between avian and seasonal influenza viruses in wastewater samples. [10.3201/eid3211.261234]

ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001). [10.1080/23744235.2026.2753489]

The optimized NA mRNA vaccines, particularly F1 and F2, provided complete protection against H3N2 challenge, reducing viral replication in the lungs and inducing detectable neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) activity against heterologous H3N2 viruses. [10.71150/jm.2609004]

key_findings_zh: 该报告详细介绍了 监测 在 2026 年第 43 周在英格兰对流感、RSV 和 COVID-19 的发现,包括急诊室就诊人数、确诊的 ARI 病例和 疫苗 吸收数据。 [news-3928ae8c980ea6f1]
针对季节性流感、新冠状病毒(COVID-19)和肺炎球菌病的疫苗接种接种活动已宣布,并计划于周一(2026-11-01)开始。该活动被确认为一项公共卫生计划,由TVMnews.mt报道。 [news-560b7b6feaf669f7]
据报道,季节性流感 会增加心脏病发作和中风的风险,特别是对于已有血管损伤或慢性疾病的个体。这得到了心脏病专家的证实并得到了研究的支持。 [news-467fad5123e6534f]
2026 年 9 月,印度尼西亚的流感病例有所增加,卫生部报告流感活动加剧。本文讨论了识别流感症状的重要性以及特定病例中医疗护理的必要性。 [news-3b84276a73493289]
流感住院人数在一周内增加了 27%,达到 6,100 人,疾病预防控制中心 (CDC) 记录了本季度首例儿童死于流感的情况。 [news-02c2de20bfe284ce]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Seasonal influenza viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: The report details the surveillance findings for influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 in England during week 43 of 2026, including ED attendances, confirmed ARI cases, and vaccine uptake data. [news-3928ae8c980ea6f1]

A vaccination campaign against seasonal influenza, COVID-19, and pneumococcal disease was announced and is set to begin on Monday, 2026-11-01. The event is confirmed as a public health initiative, reported by TVMnews.mt. [news-560b7b6feaf669f7]

Seasonal influenza is reported to increase the risk of heart attack and stroke, especially in individuals with pre-existing vascular damage or chronic illnesses. This is confirmed by cardiologists and supported by studies. [news-467fad5123e6534f]

Flu cases increased in Indonesia in September 2026, with the Ministry of Health reporting heightened influenza activity. The article discusses the importance of recognizing influenza symptoms and the need for medical attention in specific cases. [news-3b84276a73493289]
Flu hospital admissions increased by 27% in one week to 6,100, and the CDC recorded its first child death from the flu this season. [news-02c2de20bfe284ce]

papers.title: Characterization of influenza A(H3N2) viruses detected on a pig farm in Russia in 2017-2018.
papers.abstract: Pigs serve as "mixing vessels" for influenza A viruses, facilitating interspecies transmission and genomic reassortment. Here, we report characterization of influenza A(H3N2) viruses isolated from suckling and weaned piglets at one commercial pig farm in the Irkutsk Region, Russia, in August 2017 and May 2018. Full-genome sequencing revealed that their HA and NA segments clustered with human seasonal A(H3N2) strains circulating in 2002-2004, while the internal gene cassette was derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. PB1 and PB2 segments of viruses isolated in 2017 and 2018 belonged to different clusters of the A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage suggesting possible additional reassortment event. Hemagglutination inhibition assay and antigenic cartography demonstrated significant antigenic drift, with the swine isolates forming a discrete cluster ≥ 4 antigenic units distant from human seasonal A(H3N2) strains registered in 2007-2024. The viruses accumulated key substitutions, including HA1-A138S, associated with swine adaptation, yet retained full susceptibility to oseltamivir and zanamivir. Repeated detection of closely related reassortants at the same farm suggests their sustained circulation either within the farm or outside it, leading to reintroductions. Further studies are needed to understand the underlying mechanisms of this observation. Thus, our study identified a new genetic lineage of human-origin influenza A(H3N2) viruses in swine in Russia and highlighted once again that seasonal influenza viruses that stopped circulating in the human population long ago might remain undetected for years within swine and/or other unknown intermediate hosts, undergoing independent evolution and generating antigenically distinct variants that may evade pre-existing human immunity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize influenza A(H3N2) viruses detected in pigs, highlighting the role of pigs as mixing vessels for influenza A viruses and the potential for interspecies transmission and genomic reassortment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved isolating influenza A(H3N2) viruses from suckling and weaned piglets at a commercial pig farm in the Irkutsk Region, Russia, during August 2017 and May 2018.
analysis.methods: Full-genome sequencing was used to analyze the HA and NA segments, which clustered with human seasonal A(H3N2) strains from 2002-2004, while the internal gene cassette was found to be derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. Hemagglutination inhibition assay and antigenic cartography were also employed to assess antigenic drift.
analysis.main_results: The PB1 and PB2 segments of the viruses isolated in 2017 and 2018 belonged to different clusters of the A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage, suggesting a possible additional reassortment event. The swine isolates formed a discrete cluster ≥ 4 antigenic units distant from human seasonal A(H3N2) strains registered in 2007-2024.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that seasonal influenza viruses can persist in swine populations for years, undergoing independent evolution and generating antigenically distinct variants that may evade pre-existing human immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the importance of monitoring swine populations for influenza viruses, as they may serve as reservoirs for antigenically distinct variants that could potentially re-emerge in human populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study notes that further research is needed to understand the underlying mechanisms of the observed reassortment events, indicating moderate confidence in the interpretation of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized influenza A(H3N2) viruses isolated from piglets on a commercial farm in Russia during 2017-2018. It revealed that these viruses had genomic segments derived from human seasonal A(H3N2) strains of the early 2000s and internal gene cassette from A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. The PB1 and PB2 segments showed different clusters within the A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage, suggesting reassortment. Antigenic cartography indicated that the swine isolates formed a distinct cluster, ≥4 antigenic units away from human strains from 2007-2024. The study emphasizes the potential for seasonal influenza viruses to persist in swine, evolve independently, and generate variants that may evade human immunity. The findings suggest the need for continued surveillance of swine populations for influenza viruses, as they may serve as reservoirs for future human outbreaks. However, the study acknowledges the need for further research to understand the mechanisms behind the observed reassortment events, indicating moderate confidence in the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在表征在猪中检测到的流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒,强调猪作为甲型流感病毒混合容器的作用以及种间 传播 和基因组重配的潜力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2017 年 8 月和 2018 年 5 月期间从俄罗斯伊尔库茨克地区的一个商业养猪场的哺乳仔猪和断奶仔猪中分离出流感 甲型H3N2流感病毒 病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 采用全基因组测序来分析HA和NA片段,它们与2002-2004年人类季节性甲型H3N2流感病毒毒株聚类,而内部基因盒被发现源自甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09病毒。还采用血凝抑制测定和抗原制图来评估 抗原漂移。
elements_zh.main_results: 2017 年和 2018 年分离的病毒的 PB1 和 PB2 片段属于 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 谱系的不同簇,表明可能存在额外的重配事件。猪分离株形成一个离散簇,与 2007-2024 年注册的人类季节性 甲型H3N2流感病毒 菌株相距 ≥ 4 个抗原单位。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,季节性流感 病毒可以在猪群中持续存在多年,经历独立的 进化 并产生可能逃避预先存在的人类免疫力的抗原性不同的变体。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了监测猪群中流感病毒的重要性,因为它们可能作为 储存宿主 来检测可能在人类群体中重新出现的抗原性不同的变异。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究指出,需要进一步的研究来了解观察到的重配事件的潜在机制,这表明对研究结果的解释有一定的信心。

papers.title_zh: 2017-2018 年在俄罗斯养猪场检测到的 甲型H3N2流感病毒 流感病毒的特征。
papers.source_body_en: Pigs serve as "mixing vessels" for influenza A viruses, facilitating interspecies transmission and genomic reassortment. Here, we report characterization of influenza A(H3N2) viruses isolated from suckling and weaned piglets at one commercial pig farm in the Irkutsk Region, Russia, in August 2017 and May 2018. Full-genome sequencing revealed that their HA and NA segments clustered with human seasonal A(H3N2) strains circulating in 2002-2004, while the internal gene cassette was derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. PB1 and PB2 segments of viruses isolated in 2017 and 2018 belonged to different clusters of the A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage suggesting possible additional reassortment event. Hemagglutination inhibition assay and antigenic cartography demonstrated significant antigenic drift, with the swine isolates forming a discrete cluster ≥ 4 antigenic units distant from human seasonal A(H3N2) strains registered in 2007-2024. The viruses accumulated key substitutions, including HA1-A138S, associated with swine adaptation, yet retained full susceptibility to oseltamivir and zanamivir. Repeated detection of closely related reassortants at the same farm suggests their sustained circulation either within the farm or outside it, leading to reintroductions. Further studies are needed to understand the underlying mechanisms of this observation. Thus, our study identified a new genetic lineage of human-origin influenza A(H3N2) viruses in swine in Russia and highlighted once again that seasonal influenza viruses that stopped circulating in the human population long ago might remain undetected for years within swine and/or other unknown intermediate hosts, undergoing independent evolution and generating antigenically distinct variants that may evade pre-existing human immunity.

papers.title: End-of-season influenza vaccine effectiveness against a(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Beijing, China, 2025/26 season.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to estimate the end-of-season influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) against A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in the 2025/26 season in Beijing, China. METHODS: We used a test-negative design to assess influenza VE among outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) enrolled through the Beijing influenza sentinel virological surveillance system from September 2025 (week 40/2025) to May 2026 (week 21/2026). Cases were ILI patients who tested positive for influenza; controls were those who tested negative. The VE was estimated using non-conditional multiple logistic regression models, adjusting for age (modelled as a natural cubic spline), sex, presence of comorbidities, area of residence, and calendar week (modelled as a natural cubic spline). RESULTS: Among 20,749 ILI patients tested, 4875 (23.5%) were positive for influenza, with A(H3N2) and B/Victoria being the predominant strains. Adjusted VE was 26.4% (95% CI: 17.8 to 34.1) against any influenza, 22.2% (95% CI: 11.3 to 31.7) against A(H3N2), and 34.7% (95% CI: 19.6 to 47.0) against B/Victoria, with the highest VE observed in adults aged 18-59 years (53.0%, 95%CI: 37.0 to 64.9) against any influenza. The adjusted VE was similar for those vaccinated in 2025/26 only (38.7%, 95%CI: 15.6 to 55.5) or both 2024/25 and 2025/26 seasons (35.1%, 95%CI: 16.5 to 49.6), but higher than those vaccinated in 2024/25 only (17.0%, 95%CI: -16.1 to 40.7) among B/Victoria. For A(H3N2), the VE point estimate was higher among those vaccinated in the 2025/26 season only (27.9%, 95%CI: 11.5 to 41.2) than among those vaccinated in both seasons (17.9%, 95%CI: 4.0 to 29.7) and 2024/25 only (-6.1%, 95%CI: -28.7 to 12.5). CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that seasonal vaccination reduced laboratory-confirmed influenza among outpatients by approximately a quarter, with higher VE in adults aged 18-59 years. VE estimates according to vaccination status over two consecutive seasons showed different patterns for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria. These real-world findings support the ongoing public health value of influenza vaccination and highlight the importance of continuous virological surveillance, prevention, and control policy.

papers.title_zh: 2025/26 年赛季末流感 疫苗 对中国北京 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的有效性。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to estimate the end-of-season influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) against A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in the 2025/26 season in Beijing, China. METHODS: We used a test-negative design to assess influenza VE among outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) enrolled through the Beijing influenza sentinel virological surveillance system from September 2025 (week 40/2025) to May 2026 (week 21/2026). Cases were ILI patients who tested positive for influenza; controls were those who tested negative. The VE was estimated using non-conditional multiple logistic regression models, adjusting for age (modelled as a natural cubic spline), sex, presence of comorbidities, area of residence, and calendar week (modelled as a natural cubic spline). RESULTS: Among 20,749 ILI patients tested, 4875 (23.5%) were positive for influenza, with A(H3N2) and B/Victoria being the predominant strains. Adjusted VE was 26.4% (95% CI: 17.8 to 34.1) against any influenza, 22.2% (95% CI: 11.3 to 31.7) against A(H3N2), and 34.7% (95% CI: 19.6 to 47.0) against B/Victoria, with the highest VE observed in adults aged 18-59 years (53.0%, 95%CI: 37.0 to 64.9) against any influenza. The adjusted VE was similar for those vaccinated in 2025/26 only (38.7%, 95%CI: 15.6 to 55.5) or both 2024/25 and 2025/26 seasons (35.1%, 95%CI: 16.5 to 49.6), but higher than those vaccinated in 2024/25 only (17.0%, 95%CI: -16.1 to 40.7) among B/Victoria. For A(H3N2), the VE point estimate was higher among those vaccinated in the 2025/26 season only (27.9%, 95%CI: 11.5 to 41.2) than among those vaccinated in both seasons (17.9%, 95%CI: 4.0 to 29.7) and 2024/25 only (-6.1%, 95%CI: -28.7 to 12.5). CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that seasonal vaccination reduced laboratory-confirmed influenza among outpatients by approximately a quarter, with higher VE in adults aged 18-59 years. VE estimates according to vaccination status over two consecutive seasons showed different patterns for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria. These real-world findings support the ongoing public health value of influenza vaccination and highlight the importance of continuous virological surveillance, prevention, and control policy.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:本研究旨在评估中国北京 2025/26 季节末流感 疫苗 对 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的有效性 (VE)。方法:我们采用测试阴性设计来评估2025年9月(第40/2025周)至2026年5月(第21/2026周)通过北京流感哨点病毒学监测系统入组的门诊流感样疾病(ILI)患者的流感VE。病例是流感检测呈阳性的ILI患者;对照组是那些测试结果呈阴性的人。使用非条件多元逻辑回归模型估计 VE,调整年龄(建模为自然三次样条)、性别、合并症的存在、居住区域和日历周(建模为自然三次样条)。结果:在 20,749 名接受检测的 ILI 患者中,4875 名(23.5%)流感呈阳性,其中 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 是主要毒株。针对任何流感的调整后 VE 为 26.4%(95% CI:17.8 至 34.1),针对 甲型H3N2流感病毒 为 22.2%(95% CI:11.3 至 31.7),针对 B/Victoria 为 34.7%(95% CI:19.6 至 47.0),其中在 18-59 岁成年人中观察到的 VE 最高(53.0%,95%CI:37.0 至 64.9)针对任何流感。仅在 2025/26 赛季(38.7%,95%CI:15.6 至 55.5)或 2024/25 和 2025/26 赛季(35.1%,95%CI:16.5 至 49.6)接种疫苗的调整后 VE 相似,但高于仅在 2024/25 赛季接种的疫苗(17.0%,B/维多利亚州的 95%CI:-16.1 至 40.7)。对于 甲型H3N2流感病毒,仅在 2025/26 赛季接种疫苗的人(27.9%,95%CI:11.5 至 41.2)的 VE 点估计值高于在两个赛季都接种疫苗的人(17.9%,95%CI:4.0 至 29.7)和仅在 2024/25 赛季接种疫苗的人(-6.1%,95%CI:-6.1%,95%CI: -28.7 至 12.5)。结论:我们的研究结果表明,季节性 疫苗接种 使门诊患者中实验室确诊的流感减少了约四分之一,18-59 岁成年人的 VE 较高。根据连续两个赛季的 疫苗接种 状态进行的 VE 估计显示 甲型H3N2流感病毒 和 B/Victoria 的模式不同。这些现实世界的发现支持了流感 疫苗接种 的持续公共卫生价值,并强调了持续病毒学 监测、预防和控制政策的重要性。

papers.title: A Synthetic Virology Platform for Rapid Prototyping of Influenza A Virus mutants
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat, with the need for effective vaccines and antiviral therapies remaining a high priority. In vitro testing is paramount in studying novel IAV viruses and their immunogenicity. To address this need, we developed a synthetic virology approach to rapidly prototype and test IAV mutants with altered antigenic sites. By strategically inserting restriction sites within an ambisense plasmid, we generated a tool where we can seamlessly replace either 1) the full hemagglutinin (HA), 2) the HA globular head domain to generate head/stalk chimeras or 3) the five canonical antigenic sites. The cloning inserts can be computationally designed and artificially synthesized, enabling rescue of synthetic Influenza A viruses. Using this platform we rescued IAV H1N1, H3N2 & H5N1, and went on to prototype their respective antigenic site mutants & chimeric IAVs using viral genome sequence alone. This platform could be useful for generating vaccine seed strains or to study anti-viral immunity.

papers.abstract_original: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat, with the need for effective vaccines and antiviral therapies remaining a high priority. In vitro testing is paramount in studying novel IAV viruses and their immunogenicity. To address this need, we developed a synthetic virology approach to rapidly prototype and test IAV mutants with altered antigenic sites. By strategically inserting restriction sites within an ambisense plasmid, we generated a tool where we can seamlessly replace either 1) the full hemagglutinin (HA), 2) the HA globular head domain to generate head/stalk chimeras or 3) the five canonical antigenic sites. The cloning inserts can be computationally designed and artificially synthesized, enabling rescue of synthetic Influenza A viruses. Using this platform we rescued IAV H1N1, H3N2 & H5N1, and went on to prototype their respective antigenic site mutants & chimeric IAVs using viral genome sequence alone. This platform could be useful for generating vaccine seed strains or to study anti-viral immunity.

papers.title: Epitope-guided optimization improves the protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines against seasonal influenza A(H3N2) virus.
papers.abstract: Neuraminidase (NA) is increasingly recognized as a promising target antigen for improving the breadth and durability of influenza vaccines, yet NA-based mRNA vaccines remain comparatively unexplored relative to hemagglutinin-based approaches. Here, we applied a computationally guided NA antigen-design strategy to seasonal H3N2 influenza viruses and investigated whether epitope-guided optimization could improve the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines. NA-D3, an NA antigen designed based on the evolutionary characteristics of circulating H3N2 viruses, was first evaluated in an mRNA vaccine. This vaccine provided partial protection against H3N2 challenge and reduced viral replication in the lungs, although detectable neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) activity was not observed. To further improve NA antigen immunogenicity, predicted B- and T-cell epitopes were incorporated into the antigen design process, resulting in three sequentially optimized NA candidates, F0, F1, and F2. In a subsequent challenge experiment, F1 and F2 conferred complete protection, achieving 100% survival and significantly lower viral RNA levels and infectious viral titers in the lungs compared to controls. The optimized NA mRNA vaccines also induced detectable NAI activity against heterologous H3N2 viruses, albeit at relatively modest levels. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the protective potential of NA-based mRNA vaccination against H3N2 influenza viruses and establish iterative, epitope-guided strategy in NA antigen optimization - integrating computational prediction with experimental validation - as an effective approach for developing broadly protective NA-based mRNA vaccines.

papers.abstract_zh: 神经氨酸酶 (NA) 越来越被认为是一种有前景的靶抗原,可用于改善流感 疫苗 的广度和持久性,但相对于基于血凝素的方法,基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 仍未得到探索。在这里,我们将计算引导的 NA 抗原设计策略应用于季节性 H3N2 流感病毒,并研究表位引导的优化是否可以提高基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 的免疫原性和保护功效。NA-D3 是一种根据流行的 H3N2 病毒的进化特征设计的 NA 抗原,首先在 mRNA 疫苗 中进行评估。尽管没有观察到可检测的神经氨酸酶抑制 (NAI) 活性,但该 疫苗 提供了针对 H3N2 攻击的部分保护并减少了肺部病毒复制。为了进一步提高 NA 抗原的免疫原性,预测的 B 细胞和 T 细胞表位被纳入抗原设计过程中,从而产生了三个连续优化的 NA 候选物:F0、F1 和 F2。在随后的攻击实验中,F1 和 F2 提供了完全的保护,实现了 100% 的存活,并且与对照组相比,肺部的病毒 RNA 水平和传染性病毒滴度显着降低。优化的 NA mRNA 疫苗 还诱导了针对异源 H3N2 病毒的可检测 NAI 活性,尽管水平相对较低。总的来说,这些发现证明了基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗接种 对 H3N2 流感病毒的保护潜力,并在 NA 抗原优化中建立了迭代、表位引导的策略 - 将计算预测与实验验证相结合 - 作为开发广泛保护性的基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 的有效方法。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在涉及小鼠的攻击实验中评估了基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 对季节性 H3N2 流感病毒的保护功效。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员根据循环H3N2病毒的进化特征设计了NA抗原(NA-D3),并将预测的B细胞和T细胞表位纳入抗原设计过程中,依次优化了三种NA候选物(F0、F1和F2)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 优化的 NA mRNA 疫苗,特别是 F1 和 F2,提供了针对 H3N2 攻击的完全保护,减少了肺部的病毒复制,并诱导可检测到的针对异源 H3N2 病毒的神经氨酸酶抑制 (NAI) 活性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明了基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 对 H3N2 流感病毒的保护潜力,并建立了一种表位引导策略来优化 NA 抗原,将计算预测与实验验证相结合。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 优化的 NA mRNA 疫苗 有助于开发具有广泛保护性的基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗,从而增强流感 疫苗接种 策略的广度和持久性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括使用单一动物模型以及需要在人体临床试验中进一步验证。由于样本量有限且使用非人类模型,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Bovine myxovirus resistance protein (Mx)1, but not Mx2, mediates antiviral activity against human and avian influenza A viruses, including H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b.
papers.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have recently infected dairy cows in the United States, raising concerns about human spillover. The antiviral roles of bovine host defense factors, including myxovirus resistance proteins (bMx1 and bMx2), remain relatively understudied. We examined bMx1/bMx2 induction in differentiated bovine cells following HPAI H5N1 infection and assessed their antiviral activity using overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis approaches. Both bMx1 and bMx2 were more strongly induced in mammary cells than in tracheal cells. Overexpression of bMx1, but not bMx2, significantly inhibited seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs), low-pathogenic, and highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b, but not influenza B viruses. Conversely, knockdown of bMx1 resulted in enhanced IAV growth. Further, bMx1 inhibited early stages of viral replication, acting to reduce viral transcription and subsequent steps in the viral replication cycle. Known mutations that reduce human MxA (hMxA) activity also impaired bMx1 function, and mutations in the viral nucleoprotein (NP) associated with resistance to hMxA also reduced virus sensitivity to bMx1. Furthermore, phylogenetic analysis showed that a small minority (>0.03%) of avian H5N1 2.3.4.4b viruses already carry some of these NP mutations. These findings suggest that while current H5N1 viruses largely remain susceptible to bMx1, viral evolution or opportunistic reassortment could drive Mx resistance and increase pandemic risk.IMPORTANCEHighly pathogenic avian influenza viruses have spilled over into dairy cows and have been circulating on dairy farms in the United States since 2024. The innate antiviral immune responses of cows to influenza viruses have not been extensively studied. In this study, we focused on Mx proteins, a key part of the innate immune defense system toward viruses. We specifically looked at bovine Mx proteins and demonstrated antiviral activity toward different influenza viruses, including the highly pathogenic strains. We also showed that the mechanism of antiviral activity of bovine Mx1 was very similar to that of the human equivalent MxA protein. Further, we found that a small minority of these avian viruses have mutations associated with resistance to both bovine Mx1 and human MxA proteins. Overall, this work highlights the elevated pandemic risk for highly pathogenic influenza viruses through continual circulation in cows, a mammalian species in close proximity to humans.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the antiviral roles of bovine myxovirus resistance proteins (bMx1 and bMx2) in response to highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, which have recently infected dairy cows in the United States, raising concerns about human spillover. The knowledge gap lies in the understudied innate antiviral immune responses of cows to influenza viruses, particularly the roles of Mx proteins.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved examining bMx1/bMx2 induction in differentiated bovine cells following HPAI H5N1 infection and assessing their antiviral activity using overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis approaches. The research was conducted in vitro using bovine mammary and tracheal cells.
analysis.methods: The methods included examining bMx1/bMx2 induction in bovine cells, overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis of bMx1 and bMx2, and assessing antiviral activity against different influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b.
analysis.main_results: Both bMx1 and bMx2 were more strongly induced in mammary cells than in tracheal cells. Overexpression of bMx1, but not bMx2, significantly inhibited seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs), low-pathogenic, and highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b, but not influenza B viruses. Knockdown of bMx1 resulted in enhanced IAV growth. bMx1 inhibited early stages of viral replication, acting to reduce viral transcription and subsequent steps in the viral replication cycle. A small minority of avian H5N1 2.3.4.4b viruses already carry mutations that reduce MxA activity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that while current H5N1 viruses largely remain susceptible to bMx1, viral evolution or reassortment could drive Mx resistance and increase pandemic risk. The mechanism of antiviral activity of bovine Mx1 was very similar to that of the human equivalent MxA protein, and a small minority of avian viruses have mutations associated with resistance to both bovine Mx1 and human MxA proteins.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This work highlights the elevated pandemic risk for highly pathogenic influenza viruses through continual circulation in cows, a mammalian species in close proximity to humans. The findings have implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of influenza in cattle and potential human spillover events.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the in vitro nature of the experiments and the use of bovine cells, which may not fully represent the in vivo situation. The sample size for the viral mutation analysis was small, and the generalizability of the findings to other influenza viruses and species is uncertain. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: The study examined the antiviral roles of bovine myxovirus resistance proteins (bMx1 and bMx2) in response to HPAI H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses, finding that bMx1 significantly inhibited these viruses while bMx2 did not. The findings suggest potential pandemic risk due to viral evolution or reassortment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解牛粘病毒抗性蛋白(bMx1和bMx2)在应对高致病性禽流感(HPAI)H5N1分支2.3.4.4b病毒中的抗病毒药物作用,该病毒最近感染了美国的奶牛,引起了对人类跨物种溢出的担忧。知识差距在于牛对流感病毒的先天 抗病毒药物 免疫应答 的研究不足,特别是 Mx 蛋白的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及检查 HPAI H5N1 感染后分化牛细胞中 bMx1/bMx2 的诱导情况,并使用过表达、敲低和诱变方法评估其 抗病毒药物 活性。该研究是利用牛乳腺和气管细胞在体外进行的。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括检查牛细胞中的 bMx1/bMx2 诱导、bMx1 和 bMx2 的过度表达、敲低和诱变,以及评估 抗病毒药物 针对不同流感病毒(包括 H5N1 2.3.4.4b)的活性。
elements_zh.main_results: bMx1 和 bMx2 在乳腺细胞中的诱导作用比在气管细胞中的诱导作用更强。bMx1 的过表达(而非 bMx2)显着抑制 季节性流感 A 病毒 (IAV)、低致病性和高致病性禽流感病毒,包括 H5N1 2.3.4.4b,但不能抑制 B 型流感病毒。bMx1 的敲低导致 IAV 生长增强。bMx1 抑制病毒复制的早期阶段,从而减少病毒转录和病毒复制周期的后续步骤。少数禽类 H5N1 2.3.4.4b 病毒已携带可降低 MxA 活性的 突变。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,虽然目前的 H5N1 病毒在很大程度上仍然对 bMx1 敏感,但病毒 进化 或重配可能会导致 Mx 耐药性并增加大流行风险。牛Mx1的抗病毒药物活性机制与人类等效的MxA蛋白非常相似,并且少数禽类病毒具有与牛Mx1和人MxA蛋白的抗性相关的突变。

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved examining bMx1/bMx2 induction in differentiated bovine cells following HPAI H5N1 infection and assessing their antiviral activity using overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis approaches. analysis_en.methods: The methods included examining bMx1/bMx2 induction in bovine cells, overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis of bMx1 and bMx2, and assessing antiviral activity against different influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b.
analysis_en.main_results: Both bMx1 and bMx2 were more strongly induced in mammary cells than in tracheal cells. A small minority of avian H5N1 2.3.4.4b viruses already carry mutations that reduce MxA activity.

The mechanism of antiviral activity of bovine Mx1 was very similar to that of the human equivalent MxA protein, and a small minority of avian viruses have mutations associated with resistance to both bovine Mx1 and human MxA proteins.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This work highlights the elevated pandemic risk for highly pathogenic influenza viruses through continual circulation in cows, a mammalian species in close proximity to humans. papers.title_zh: 牛粘病毒抗性蛋白 (Mx)1(而非 Mx2)介导 抗病毒药物 针对人类和禽甲型流感病毒(包括 H5N1 进化枝 2.3.4.4b)的活性。
papers.source_body_en: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have recently infected dairy cows in the United States, raising concerns about human spillover. The antiviral roles of bovine host defense factors, including myxovirus resistance proteins (bMx1 and bMx2), remain relatively understudied. We examined bMx1/bMx2 induction in differentiated bovine cells following HPAI H5N1 infection and assessed their antiviral activity using overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis approaches. Both bMx1 and bMx2 were more strongly induced in mammary cells than in tracheal cells. Overexpression of bMx1, but not bMx2, significantly inhibited seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs), low-pathogenic, and highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b, but not influenza B viruses. Conversely, knockdown of bMx1 resulted in enhanced IAV growth. Further, bMx1 inhibited early stages of viral replication, acting to reduce viral transcription and subsequent steps in the viral replication cycle. Known mutations that reduce human MxA (hMxA) activity also impaired bMx1 function, and mutations in the viral nucleoprotein (NP) associated with resistance to hMxA also reduced virus sensitivity to bMx1. Furthermore, phylogenetic analysis showed that a small minority (>0.03%) of avian H5N1 2.3.4.4b viruses already carry some of these NP mutations. These findings suggest that while current H5N1 viruses largely remain susceptible to bMx1, viral evolution or opportunistic reassortment could drive Mx resistance and increase pandemic risk.IMPORTANCEHighly pathogenic avian influenza viruses have spilled over into dairy cows and have been circulating on dairy farms in the United States since 2024. The innate antiviral immune responses of cows to influenza viruses have not been extensively studied. In this study, we focused on Mx proteins, a key part of the innate immune defense system toward viruses. We specifically looked at bovine Mx proteins and demonstrated antiviral activity toward different influenza viruses, including the highly pathogenic strains. We also showed that the mechanism of antiviral activity of bovine Mx1 was very similar to that of the human equivalent MxA protein. Further, we found that a small minority of these avian viruses have mutations associated with resistance to both bovine Mx1 and human MxA proteins. Overall, this work highlights the elevated pandemic risk for highly pathogenic influenza viruses through continual circulation in cows, a mammalian species in close proximity to humans.

papers.title: ADAR-mediated RNA editing of Influenza A virus genomes may be age-dependent and inversely correlates with viral load.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza epidemics cause significant mortality, especially among the elderly. Influenza A virus triggers the host innate immune system through various mechanisms. Human enzymes belonging to the group of RNA-acting adenosine deaminases (ADARs) play a role in the innate antiviral immune response, partly by inducing mutations in viral RNA. The effect of this mechanismin influenza A virus infection remains unexplained in humans. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the clinical impact of ADAR-induced mutations on influenza A virus in hospitalised patients. METHODS: Full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus was performed on respiratory samples from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years. ADAR-associated mutations in minor viral subpopulations were analysed in relation to demographic and clinical factors. RESULTS: ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: We found an association between ADAR-induced mutations and viral load, which may indicate an antiviral function of ADAR on influenza A virus. The lower mutation rate and associated higher viral load in the elderly suggest an age-dependent reduced ADAR activity, which may contribute to increased disease severity.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the clinical impact of ADAR-induced mutations on influenza A virus in hospitalised patients, addressing the unexplained effect of this mechanism in humans. Seasonal influenza epidemics cause significant mortality, especially among the elderly, and influenza A virus triggers the host innate immune system through various mechanisms. Human enzymes, such as ADARs, play a role in the innate antiviral immune response by inducing mutations in viral RNA.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years, to analyse ADAR-associated mutations in relation to demographic and clinical factors.
elements_en.methods: Full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus was performed on respiratory samples from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years. ADAR-associated mutations in minor viral subpopulations were analysed in relation to demographic and clinical factors.
elements_en.main_results: ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: We found an association between ADAR-induced mutations and viral load, which may indicate an antiviral function of ADAR on influenza A virus. The lower mutation rate and associated higher viral load in the elderly suggest an age-dependent reduced ADAR activity, which may contribute to increased disease severity.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that ADAR activity may play a role in the clinical outcome of influenza A virus infection, particularly in the elderly. This could inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for influenza, especially in high-risk populations.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the small sample size and the focus on a single influenza A(H3N2) strain. The findings may not be generalisable to other influenza strains or populations. The study design does not allow for causal inference, and the results are based on observational data.

papers.title_zh: ADAR 介导的甲型流感病毒 基因组 的 RNA 编辑可能具有年龄依赖性,并且与病毒载量呈负相关。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza epidemics cause significant mortality, especially among the elderly. Influenza A virus triggers the host innate immune system through various mechanisms. Human enzymes belonging to the group of RNA-acting adenosine deaminases (ADARs) play a role in the innate antiviral immune response, partly by inducing mutations in viral RNA. The effect of this mechanismin influenza A virus infection remains unexplained in humans. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the clinical impact of ADAR-induced mutations on influenza A virus in hospitalised patients. METHODS: Full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus was performed on respiratory samples from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years. ADAR-associated mutations in minor viral subpopulations were analysed in relation to demographic and clinical factors. RESULTS: ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: We found an association between ADAR-induced mutations and viral load, which may indicate an antiviral function of ADAR on influenza A virus. The lower mutation rate and associated higher viral load in the elderly suggest an age-dependent reduced ADAR activity, which may contribute to increased disease severity.

papers.title: Influenza A Virus at the Exhibition Swine‐Human Interface in the USA
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: In the USA, zoonotic influenza A virus (IAV) transmission occurs frequently in youth who exhibit swine at agricultural competitions, presenting an ongoing pandemic risk. However, active surveillance in this high-risk human population is lacking. METHODS: To address this gap, we enrolled 711 youth participants at nine swine exhibitions during 2019-2021 and collected 700 nasal swabs and 400 serum samples. We assessed the neutralizing antibody titers of enrollees against eight influenza A H1 and H3 variant candidate vaccine viruses (CVVs) recommended by the World Health Organization. RESULTS: We found that the highest neutralizing titers are not necessarily associated with the specific viruses which are most prevalent in exhibition swine during the same time period. The geometric mean titers of the cohort were low against the Cluster IV-A (clade 3.1990.4.a) CVV, which we determined to be the most prevalent HA lineage circulating in exhibition swine during 2020-2021 based on simultaneous IAV surveillance in swine (n = 430 genome sequences). CONCLUSIONS: The relatively low neutralizing antibody levels in this high-risk population with intense exposure to livestock indicates that sustained outreach and monitoring is needed. Continued monitoring of IAVs in both swine and humans can inform viral risk assessments and provide considerations for candidate vaccine virus selection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the transmission of influenza A virus (IAV) among youth participants at swine exhibitions in the USA, highlighting the risk of zoonotic spread. The research aimed to assess neutralizing antibody titers against eight influenza A H1 and H3 variant candidate vaccine viruses (CVVs) recommended by the World Health Organization. The study collected nasal swabs and serum samples from 711 participants across nine exhibitions between 2019 and 2021. Results showed that the highest neutralizing titers were not linked to the most prevalent IAV strains in swine during the same period. The authors interpreted these findings as indicating a need for sustained outreach and monitoring in this high-risk population. papers.title_zh: 美国猪人界面展览会上的甲型流感病毒
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: In the USA, zoonotic influenza A virus (IAV) transmission occurs frequently in youth who exhibit swine at agricultural competitions, presenting an ongoing pandemic risk. However, active surveillance in this high-risk human population is lacking. METHODS: To address this gap, we enrolled 711 youth participants at nine swine exhibitions during 2019-2021 and collected 700 nasal swabs and 400 serum samples. We assessed the neutralizing antibody titers of enrollees against eight influenza A H1 and H3 variant candidate vaccine viruses (CVVs) recommended by the World Health Organization. RESULTS: We found that the highest neutralizing titers are not necessarily associated with the specific viruses which are most prevalent in exhibition swine during the same time period. The geometric mean titers of the cohort were low against the Cluster IV-A (clade 3.1990.4.a) CVV, which we determined to be the most prevalent HA lineage circulating in exhibition swine during 2020-2021 based on simultaneous IAV surveillance in swine (n = 430 genome sequences). CONCLUSIONS: The relatively low neutralizing antibody levels in this high-risk population with intense exposure to livestock indicates that sustained outreach and monitoring is needed. Continued monitoring of IAVs in both swine and humans can inform viral risk assessments and provide considerations for candidate vaccine virus selection.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:在美国,人畜共患甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 传播 经常发生在在农业竞赛中展示猪的青少年中,存在持续的大流行风险。然而,这一高危人群缺乏活跃的 监测。方法:为了弥补这一差距,我们在 2019-2021 年期间招募了 9 场生猪展览的 711 名青年参与者,并收集了 700 份鼻拭子和 400 份血清样本。我们评估了参与者针对世界卫生组织推荐的八种甲型流感 H1 和 H3 变异候选 疫苗 病毒 (CVV) 的中和抗体滴度。结果:我们发现最高的中和滴度不一定与同一时期展览猪中最流行的特定病毒相关。队列研究 的几何平均滴度相对于 IV-A 簇(进化枝 3.1990.4.a)CVV 较低,我们根据猪中同步 IAV 监测(n = 430 基因组 序列)确定该簇是 2020-2021 年展览猪中最流行的 HA 谱系。结论:在这一频繁接触牲畜的高危人群中,中和抗体水平相对较低,表明需要持续的外展和监测。对猪和人类 IAV 的持续监测可以为病毒风险评估提供信息,并为候选 疫苗 病毒的选择提供考虑因素。

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening of cyanobacterial metabolites against key influenza A virus targets
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a major threat to global health and livestock industries, necessitating the discovery of new antiviral agents. In this study, a structure-based virtual screening of 1288 cyanobacterial secondary metabolites was performed against key IAV proteins, including hemagglutinin (H3 and H5), neuraminidase (N1 and N2), and RNA polymerase subunits (PB2 and PA). Molecular docking was conducted using AutoDock Vina with a rigid receptor–flexible ligand approach, and binding conformations were evaluated based on docking scores, molecular size, binding orientation, and interactions with functionally critical residues. A multi-target docking strategy combined with multiple docking-related criteria identified several promising candidates with more favorable predicted docking scores than the corresponding native ligands for H3, H5, N1, and N2, but slightly less favorable scores for PB2 and PA. Key compounds included 11,12-didehydrospironostoic acid, 7-formyl-3-methoxy-5-methylindanone, mycosporine-glycine-alanine, palythine-serine, Asterina-330, toyocamycin, usujirene, tjipanazole derivatives, tubercidin, and didmolamide A. Notably, among the prioritized compounds, metabolites from Calothrix exhibited the broadest predicted multi-target binding profile, followed by Tolypothrix , while compounds derived from Lyngbya/Moorea , Scytonema , Leptolyngbya , Nostoc , and Fischerella demonstrated target-specific or limited multi-target binding profiles. Scaffold-based analysis revealed key structural classes, including nucleoside-like compounds, mycosporine-like amino acids, and peptide/alkaloid derivatives, contributing to favorable predicted binding interactions with functionally critical residues. ADMET evaluation revealed variable predicted pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles among the prioritized compounds, with several candidates exhibiting low predicted intestinal absorption or elevated mutagenicity risk, highlighting the need for further safety and pharmacokinetic evaluation. Overall, this study highlights cyanobacterial metabolites as a structurally diverse and underexplored source of potential multi-target antiviral candidates against IAV and provides a framework for future computational refinement and experimental validation toward applications in both human and animal health.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 仍然是全球健康和畜牧业的主要威胁,因此需要发现新的 抗病毒药物 制剂。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项研究中,针对关键 IAV 蛋白,包括血凝素(H3 和 H5)、神经氨酸酶(N1 和 N2)和 RNA 聚合酶亚基(PB2 和 PA),对 1288 种蓝藻次生代谢物进行了基于结构的虚拟筛选。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 AutoDock Vina 和刚性受体-柔性配体方法进行分子对接,并根据对接分数、分子大小、结合方向以及与功能关键残基的相互作用来评估结合构象。
elements_zh.main_results: 多目标对接策略与多个对接相关标准相结合,确定了几种有前途的候选物,其预测对接分数比 H3、H5、N1 和 N2 的相应天然配体更有利,但 PB2 和 PA 的分数稍差。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 基于支架的分析揭示了关键的结构类别,包括核苷样化合物、菌孢素样氨基酸和肽/生物碱衍生物,有助于预测与功能关键残基的良好预测结合相互作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: ADMET 评估揭示了优先化合物中不同的预测药代动力学和毒性特征,其中几种候选化合物表现出预测肠道吸收低或致突变风险升高,这突出表明需要进一步进行安全性和药代动力学评估。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告本研究的局限性或证据强度。

papers.title: Cross-reactivity against drifted influenza A (H3N2) subclade K is predicted by pre-existing antibody signatures from recent vaccine targets
papers.abstract: Abstract Seasonal influenza vaccine strains are selected months before the flu season begins, risking a vaccine mismatch. To that end, quickly predicting protection against newly emerged influenza strains is a public health preparedness need. Further, understanding immunological correlates of protection against mismatched targets is necessary for improving annual influenza vaccination compositions and/or platforms. Using a modified systems-predicted neutralizing antibody (SNAb) approach, we quantified predicted influenza virus neutralization responses in a human cohort pre- and post-vaccination during the 2025/2026 influenza season, during which the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K accounted for most influenza virus infections. This was done using the previous 10 years of vaccine targets, including the components of the 2025/2026 vaccination, as well as the 2026/2027 vaccine targets. We identified that H3N2 subclade K responders were predicted by baseline SNAb profiles, particularly to the H3N2 components of the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza vaccine. Systems serological analysis supported this at the multivariate level, with even greater accuracy in predicting mismatched responses from pre-vaccination humoral signatures. Lastly, we employed this approach to predict who would likely be high responders to the 2026/2027 influenza vaccine H1 component, and found that antibody features selected as predicting a strong neutralization response were disproportionately enriched for the H1 component of the 2025/2026 influenza vaccination. Our results support a model in which systems-based approaches can identify signatures predicting strong influenza vaccination responses before the influenza season begins.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Seasonal influenza vaccine strains are selected months before the flu season begins, risking a vaccine mismatch. This study aimed to address the need for predicting protection against newly emerged influenza strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a modified systems-predicted neutralizing antibody (SNAb) approach to quantify predicted influenza virus neutralization responses in a human cohort pre- and post-vaccination during the 2025/2026 influenza season, when the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K accounted for most influenza virus infections.
analysis.methods: Using a modified systems-predicted neutralizing antibody (SNAb) approach, the researchers quantified predicted influenza virus neutralization responses in a human cohort before and after vaccination during the 2025/2026 influenza season, which was dominated by the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K.
analysis.main_results: The study identified that H3N2 subclade K responders were predicted by baseline SNAb profiles, particularly to the H3N2 components of the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that systems-based serological analysis can predict mismatched responses from pre-vaccination humoral signatures, supporting a model for identifying vaccination response signatures before the influenza season begins.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform the development of systems-based approaches to improve influenza vaccine composition and predict individual responses to mismatched vaccine targets, enhancing public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by its reliance on a single influenza season's data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of systems-based serological analysis to predict immune responses against the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K during the 2025/2026 influenza season. The researchers used a modified SNAb approach to assess pre- and post-vaccination neutralization responses in a human cohort. They found that baseline SNAb profiles, particularly those targeting H3N2 components of previous vaccines, could predict responses to the mismatched subclade K. These results suggest that such systems-based methods can identify signatures that predict strong influenza vaccination responses before the season begins, offering a potential tool for improving vaccine composition and public health preparedness. However, the study's findings are based on a single season's data and may be subject to unmeasured confounding factors, limiting the generalizability of the results.

papers.title: S100A4 facilitates influenza A virus replication by interacting with M2 in human alveolar epithelial cells
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) replication depends on host cells and is regulated by numerous host factors. Therefore, investigating and understanding the role of these host factors is a significant topic. In this study, we found the IAV replication was attenuated after host factor S100 calcium-binding protein A4 (S100A4) was knocked down with RNAi or knockout with CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technology. Conversely, IAV replication was enhanced upon the overexpression in A549 cells. The interaction between S100A4 and the IAV M2 protein was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation. Meanwhile, confocal microscopy experiment demonstrated that the viral M2 protein co-localized with endogenous S100A4 in IAV-infected A549 cells. Truncation analysis confirmed that amino acids 45–62 of the M2 protein constitute the main interaction region with S100A4. Further study showed that viral entry was reduced after S100A4 deletion. And the polymerase activity was significantly decreased in S100A4-knockout A549 cells compared to that in wild-type A549 cells. The S100A4 overexpression resulted in the downregulation of IFN-β, while the mRNA levels of the interferon-stimulated genes ISG15 and BST2 were also significantly reduced. Therefore, the host factor S100A4 was a positive modulator of IAV replication and was involved in the viral entry, polymerase activity maintenance and innate immune regulation. Collectively, our findings shed new light on the molecular mechanisms governing IAV infection and suggest a previously underexplored avenue for antiviral therapeutic intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the host factor S100A4 in influenza A virus (IAV) replication. The researchers found that knocking down or knocking out S100A4 in human alveolar epithelial cells (A549) attenuated IAV replication, while overexpression enhanced it. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed the interaction between S100A4 and the IAV M2 protein, and confocal microscopy showed their co-localization in infected cells. Truncation analysis identified the main interaction region of the M2 protein with S100A4. Further results indicated that S100A4 deletion reduced viral entry and significantly decreased polymerase activity. The study also found that S100A4 overexpression downregulated IFN-β and interferon-stimulated genes ISG15 and BST2. These findings suggest that S100A4 is a positive modulator of IAV replication, involved in viral entry, polymerase activity maintenance, and innate immune regulation. The study provides insights into the molecular mechanisms of IAV infection and highlights a potential target for antiviral interventions. However, the study was conducted in vitro, which may limit its applicability to in vivo conditions, and the evidence strength is moderate.

papers.title: Identification of cis-Acting Elements that Regulate Influenza A Virus Segment 7 Differential mRNA Splicing
papers.abstract: Influenza A virus segment 7 encodes the M1 matrix protein and M2 ion channel from an unspliced primary transcript (mRNA1) and spliced mRNA2, respectively. Both proteins are essential for efficient virus replication, but the intrinsic sequences that determine segment 7 splicing balance are not fully defined. Here, we systematically investigated how conserved cis-acting splicing elements regulate segment splicing. We found that while the splice acceptor sequence is optimal, both potential upstream polypyrimidine tracts regulate splicing, with the 5' region acting positively and the 3' region negatively to maintain M1 expression. Nucleotide A713 is the most likely mRNA2 branch point, but potentially with redundancy from other local adenosines. Mutagenesis of the mRNA2 splice donor sequence showed that it is nearly optimal but that nucleotides 51 and 55 modestly downregulate splicing efficiency. Most introduced mutations that change splicing balance are nonsynonymous in M1. Nevertheless, polypyrimidine tract and branch point mutations that significantly perturbed M1:M2 balance resulted in viable viruses. In contrast, the splice donor sequence was largely intolerant of mutation. We conclude that M1:M2 balance is maintained via suboptimal splice donor and polypyrimidine tract splicing signals, with the latter allowing more evolutionary flexibility to vary the ratio and/or M1 sequence

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify cis-acting elements that regulate differential mRNA splicing of influenza A virus segment 7, which encodes the M1 matrix protein and M2 ion channel from unspliced and spliced transcripts, respectively. The research was motivated by the need to understand the intrinsic sequences that determine the splicing balance between these two proteins.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a systematic investigation of how conserved cis-acting splicing elements regulate segment 7 splicing in influenza A virus. It focused on the balance between M1 and M2 expression, with no specific mention of study dates, centres, or sample size.
analysis.methods: The researchers performed mutagenesis of the mRNA2 splice donor sequence and analyzed the effects on splicing efficiency. They also examined the roles of potential upstream polypyrimidine tracts and the branch point in regulating splicing balance.
analysis.main_results: Mutagenesis of the mRNA2 splice donor sequence showed that it is nearly optimal, but nucleotides 51 and 55 modestly downregulate splicing efficiency. Additionally, the 5' region of the polypyrimidine tract acts positively, while the 3' region acts negatively to maintain M1 expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the M1:M2 balance is maintained through suboptimal splice donor and polypyrimidine tract splicing signals, with the latter providing more evolutionary flexibility to vary the ratio and/or M1 sequence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms that regulate mRNA splicing in influenza A virus, which could inform future studies on viral gene expression and potentially contribute to the development of targeted antiviral strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence and does not include detailed experimental results or statistical analyses. The evidence strength is moderate as the conclusions are based on mutagenesis and splicing signal analysis without further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the cis-acting elements that regulate differential mRNA splicing of influenza A virus segment 7, which encodes the M1 matrix protein and M2 ion channel. The research highlights the roles of the splice donor sequence and polypyrimidine tracts in maintaining the M1:M2 balance. The findings suggest that the balance is achieved through suboptimal splicing signals, with the polypyrimidine tract allowing more evolutionary flexibility. The study is based on mutagenesis experiments and abstract-level evidence, which provides moderate confidence in the conclusions. These results could inform future research on viral gene expression and potentially contribute to antiviral strategies.

papers.title: Influenza B Circulation and Vaccine Effectiveness Against Medically Attended Outpatient Influenza B Illness, United States, 2016-17 Through 2024-25.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza B vaccine effectiveness (VE) has varied by season, lineage, antigenic drift, and vaccine composition. After B/Yamagata detection ceased globally, trivalent vaccines containing B/Victoria were reintroduced in 2024-25. We evaluated influenza B circulation and VE across eight analyzed seasons spanning this transition. METHODS: Ambulatory patients aged ≥6 months with acute respiratory illness were enrolled at U.S. Flu VE Network sites during eight influenza seasons from 2016-17 through 2024-25; 2020-21 was excluded because influenza circulation was negligible. Participants were tested by RT-PCR. Lineage-specific VE was estimated using a test-negative design and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, calendar time, and study site. VE was reported for season-lineage strata with ≥50 influenza B cases. RESULTS: Among 65,773 participants, 3,629 influenza B cases were included in lineage-specific VE analyses (1,507 B/Yamagata; 2,122 B/Victoria). Six of 10 season-lineage strata met the reporting threshold. B/Victoria VE was 58% (95% CI, 28%-77%) in 2016-17, 51% (43%-57%) in 2019-20, 78% (71%-84%) in 2023-24, and 39% (14%-56%) in 2024-25. B/Yamagata VE was 55% (46%-63%) in 2016-17 and 49% (40%-56%) in 2017-18. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza vaccines protected against medically attended outpatient influenza B illness, although VE varied by season. Continued VE monitoring and genetic surveillance are needed to detect emerging influenza B viruses and inform vaccine strain selection.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated influenza B vaccine effectiveness (VE) across eight seasons from 2016-17 to 2024-25, focusing on the transition from B/Yamagata to B/Victoria lineages. The research aimed to understand how VE varied by season and lineage, with the goal of informing vaccine strain selection. The study used a test-negative design and logistic regression to estimate VE, adjusting for demographic and temporal factors. Results showed that VE varied significantly across different season-lineage strata, with notable effectiveness against B/Victoria in some years and lower effectiveness against B/Yamagata in others. The findings highlight the importance of ongoing VE monitoring and genetic surveillance to adapt to changing influenza B virus patterns. The study's evidence is moderate, as it is based on an abstract-only review and does not provide detailed limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: B 型流感 疫苗 有效性 (VE) 因季节、谱系、抗原漂移 和 疫苗 成分而异。B/Yamagata 在全球范围内停止检测后,含有 B/Victoria 的三价 疫苗 于 2024-25 年重新引入。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们评估了跨越这一转变的八个分析季节的乙型流感循环和 VE。在 2016-17 年至 2024-25 年的八个流感季节期间,美国流感 VE 网络站点招募了年龄≥6 个月的患有急性呼吸道疾病的门诊患者;2020-21 年被排除在外,因为流感传播量可以忽略不计。
elements_zh.methods: 参与者接受了 RT-PCR 测试。使用测试阴性设计和针对年龄、性别、种族/民族、日历时间和研究地点进行调整的逻辑回归来估计谱系特异性 VE。
elements_zh.main_results: VE 报告为≥50 例乙型流感病例的季节谱系层。在 65,773 名参与者中,3,629 例乙型流感病例被纳入谱系特异性 VE 分析(1,507 例 B/山形;2,122 例 B/维多利亚)。10 个季节谱系阶层中有 6 个达到了报告门槛。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管 VE 随季节变化,但流感 疫苗 可以预防门诊 B 型流感疾病。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 需要持续的 VE 监测和遗传 监测 来检测新出现的乙型流感病毒并为 疫苗 毒株选择提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体局限性。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:流感B病毒株的疫苗有效性(VE)在不同季节、谱系、抗原漂移和疫苗组成方面有所不同。在B/Yamagata病毒株全球检测停止后,含有B/Victoria病毒株的三价疫苗于2024-25赛季重新引入。我们评估了流感B病毒的传播情况以及在这一转变期间的八个分析季节中的疫苗有效性。方法:在2016-17至2024-25年的八个流感季节中,美国流感疫苗有效性网络站点招募了年龄≥6个月且患有急性呼吸道疾病的门诊患者;由于2020-21年流感传播量极少,该年份被排除。参与者通过RT-PCR进行检测。使用测试阴性设计和调整年龄、性别、种族/民族、日历时间和研究地点的逻辑回归分析,估计了特定谱系的疫苗有效性。对于流感B病例≥50的季节-谱系分层,报告了疫苗有效性结果。结果:在65,773名参与者中,有3,629例流感B病例纳入谱系特异性疫苗有效性分析(1,507例B/Yamagata;2,122例B/Victoria)。10个季节-谱系分层中有6个达到报告阈值。2016-17年B/Victoria病毒株的疫苗有效性为58%(95%置信区间,28%-77%),2019-20年为51%(43%-57%),2023-24年为78%(71%-84%),2024-25年为39%(14%-56%)。2016-17年和2017-18年B/Yamagata病毒株的疫苗有效性分别为55%(46%-63%)和49%(40%-56%)。结论:流感疫苗对需要医疗干预的流感B门诊病例提供了保护,尽管疫苗有效性在不同季节有所变化。需要持续监测疫苗有效性并进行遗传监测,以检测新兴的流感B病毒株并为疫苗株选择提供信息。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: B 型流感 疫苗 有效性 (VE) 因季节、谱系、抗原漂移 和 疫苗 成分而异。B/Yamagata 在全球范围内停止检测后,含有 B/Victoria 的三价 疫苗 于 2024-25 年重新引入。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们评估了跨越这一转变的八个分析季节的乙型流感循环和 VE。在 2016-17 年至 2024-25 年的八个流感季节期间,美国流感 VE 网络站点招募了年龄≥6 个月的患有急性呼吸道疾病的门诊患者;2020-21 年被排除在外,因为流感传播量可以忽略不计。
analysis_zh.methods: 参与者接受了 RT-PCR 测试。使用测试阴性设计和针对年龄、性别、种族/民族、日历时间和研究地点进行调整的逻辑回归来估计谱系特异性 VE。
analysis_zh.main_results: VE 报告为≥50 例乙型流感病例的季节谱系层。在 65,773 名参与者中,3,629 例乙型流感病例被纳入谱系特异性 VE 分析(1,507 例 B/山形;2,122 例 B/维多利亚)。10 个季节谱系阶层中有 6 个达到了报告门槛。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管 VE 随季节变化,但流感 疫苗 可以预防门诊 B 型流感疾病。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 需要持续的 VE 监测和遗传 监测 来检测新出现的乙型流感病毒并为 疫苗 毒株选择提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体局限性。

papers.title: More Shots on Goal: Heterologous Influenza Prime-Boost Vaccination Decreases the Likelihood of a Negligible Antibody Response to Current or Historical Variants
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccination only elicits a strong and durable antibody response in a subset of recipients, and prior homologous booster trials have failed to improve on single-dose vaccination. Here, we conducted a phase 4 clinical trial to test if a heterologous prime-boost increases antibody magnitude or breadth as well as reduces the rate of non-responders (ClinicalTrials.gov ID# NCT06567860). Participants received a late-season 2023 inactivated influenza vaccine followed by the 2024 booster four months later containing an updated H3N2 strain alongside unchanged H1N1 and B/Victoria strains, allowing within-subject comparison of heterologous and homologous boosting. The booster vaccination halted or reversed antibody titer waning for all vaccine strains, most notably restoring seroprotective and seroconverting titers for B/Victoria at the cohort-level. Critically, the heterologous booster decreased the rate of non-responders (exhibiting HAI[≤]10 at all time points), with 0% H3N2 non-responders among subjects receiving the prime and boost compared to 29% H1N1 non-responders. A similar pattern held in a larger cohort administering consecutive fall vaccinations, where non-response rate was 20% of H3N2 compared to 37% for H1N1. Across all non-responders that had consistently low titers against the vaccine strains, up to half elicited an antibody response against historical variants, suggesting that immune imprinting partially underlies the non-responder phenotype. Despite differing vaccination timing, late-season priming and standard fall vaccination produced comparable antibody breadth 30 days post-vaccination when cohorts were matched on pre-vaccination titers. These findings suggest that heterologous vaccinations or other multi-strain exposures can reduce the fraction of the population that does not mount an antibody response during an influenza season.

papers.title: Sequence-structured fitness landscapes predict influenza evolution
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza viruses continually evolve to evade host immunity. Vaccines must be regularly updated to protect against new circulating strains, motivating efforts to forecast viral evolution. Recent experimental and computational methods have made progress on this problem, but learning the fitness landscape driving viral evolution remains challenging because genomic surveillance samples only a small fraction of the possible sequence space. Here, we developed a generative framework that shares information across genetically related variants, inferring effective mutation-level contributions to viral fitness from temporal sequence data. Applied to hemagglutinin and neuraminidase from A/H3N2 and A/H1N1 viruses, the inferred fitness landscapes recovers known determinants of antigenicity and reveals convergent spatial organization across subtypes consistent with common antibody-mediated selection. Forward simulations from these landscapes predicted both the fixation or loss of circulating mutations and the future composition of viral populations, outperforming models based on neutral evolution or multinomial-logistic growth. Collectively, our results show that interpretable representations of pathogen fitness landscapes can reveal biologically important features and improve prospective evolutionary forecasting.

papers.title: Temporal Shifting of Influenza Subtype Dynamics in Pakistan Following the COVID-19 Pandemic: A 10-Year FluNet Analysis, 2015-2024.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated nonpharmaceutical interventions caused unprecedented suppression of influenza circulation globally. Pakistan, with its high population density and evolving surveillance capacity, lacks long-term data on post-COVID-19 influenza patterns, essential for guiding vaccine policy. METHODS: We extracted weekly virological data for Pakistan from the WHO FluNet platform (January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024). The study period was divided into pre-COVID-19 (2015-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 (2022-2024) phases. Outcomes included type A versus B proportion, subtype distribution (A[H1N1]pdm09 vs. A[H3]), positivity, peak intensity, and season duration (weeks with positivity ≥ 10%). Statistical comparisons used chi-square for subtype distribution and Kruskal-Wallis for peak intensity. RESULTS: We analyzed 6522 positive specimens from 79,484 tested (10,781 pre-COVID-19; 14,687 during COVID-19 disruption; 54,016 post-COVID-19). Influenza A declined from 94.2% to 71.7% then rose to 77.5%; influenza B increased from 5.7% to 28.3%, remaining at 22.5% (p < 0.001). A(H3) dominated during the COVID-19 disruption (98.8%); A(H1N1)pdm09 regained dominance post-COVID-19 (58.8%), though A(H3) remained higher than pre-COVID-19 (41.2% vs. Peak intensity differed (p = 0.047): pre-COVID-19 33.3%-67.6%; COVID-19 disruption 14.0%-17.6%; and post-COVID-19 19.8%-37.8%. Season duration was 1 week in 2020 and 3 non-consecutive weeks in 2021, versus 10-16 weeks pre-COVID-19, recovering to 7-13 weeks post-COVID-19. CONCLUSION: The COVID-19 pandemic induced a lasting shift in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, with persistently elevated influenza B and reshaped A subtype balance. These findings are consistent with the global disappearance of B/Yamagata and support consideration of trivalent vaccine formulations, though antigenic and genetic data remain necessary to confirm vaccine match.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how the COVID-19 pandemic affected influenza circulation in Pakistan, particularly focusing on the shift in subtype dynamics. The background highlights that the pandemic and its interventions led to a global suppression of influenza activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed weekly virological data from the WHO FluNet platform in Pakistan, covering the period from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024. It divided the data into three phases: pre-COVID-19 (2015-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 (2022-2024).
analysis.methods: The researchers extracted virological data and categorized outcomes such as subtype distribution, positivity, peak intensity, and season duration. They used chi-square tests for subtype distribution and Kruskal-Wallis tests for peak intensity comparisons.
analysis.main_results: The study found that influenza A declined from 94.2% to 71.7% during the pandemic and then increased to 77.5%. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the pandemic caused a lasting shift in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, with increased influenza B and changes in the balance between A subtypes. This aligns with global trends of B/Yamagata disappearance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that vaccine policy in Pakistan should consider the altered influenza dynamics, particularly the increased prevalence of influenza B and the need for trivalent vaccine formulations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only data, which may limit the depth of analysis. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on observational trends without detailed mechanistic or causal explanations.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on influenza dynamics in Pakistan using a 10-year dataset from the WHO FluNet platform. It identifies a significant shift in the proportion of influenza A and B subtypes, with influenza B increasing and A(H1N1)pdm09 regaining dominance post-pandemic. The findings suggest a lasting change in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, consistent with global trends of B/Yamagata decline. These results have implications for vaccine formulation and policy, though further antigenic and genetic data are needed to confirm vaccine match. The study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on observational data without detailed causal mechanisms.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:COVID-19 大流行和相关的非药物干预措施导致全球流感传播受到前所未有的抑制。巴基斯坦人口密度高,监测 能力不断发展,缺乏有关 COVID-19 后流感模式的长期数据,而这对于指导 疫苗 政策至关重要。方法:我们从 WHO FluNet 平台(2015 年 1 月 1 日至 2024 年 12 月 31 日)提取了巴基斯坦每周的病毒学数据。研究时期分为COVID-19之前(2015-2019)、COVID-19中断(2020-2021)和COVID-19之后(2022-2024)阶段。结果包括 A 型与 B 型比例、亚型分布(A[H1N1]pdm09 与 A[H3])、阳性率、峰值强度和季节持续时间(阳性率≥ 10% 的周数)。统计比较使用卡方进行亚型分布,使用 Kruskal-Wallis 进行峰值强度。结果:我们分析了 79,484 份检测中的 6522 份阳性样本(10,781 份在 COVID-19 之前;14,687 份在 COVID-19 中断期间;54,016 份在 COVID-19 后)。甲型流感从 94.2% 下降至 71.7%,然后上升至 77.5%;乙型流感从 5.7% 增加至 28.3%,维持在 22.5% (p < 0.001)。A(H3) 在 COVID-19 干扰期间占主导地位 (98.8%);甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 在 COVID-19 后重新占据主导地位 (58.8%),但 A(H3) 仍高于 COVID-19 前(41.2% 与峰值强度不同 (p = 0.047):COVID-19 前 33.3%-67.6%;COVID-19 中断 14.0%-17.6%;以及 COVID-19 后19.8%-37.8%。2020 年季节持续时间为 1 周,2021 年为非连续的 3 周,而 COVID-19 之前为 10-16 周,恢复到 COVID-19 后 7-13 周。结论:COVID-19 大流行导致巴基斯坦流感 流行病学 持续升高,并重塑了 A 亚型平衡。与 B/Yamagata 的全球消失一致,并支持考虑三价 疫苗 制剂,尽管仍需要抗原和遗传数据来确认 疫苗 匹配。

papers.title: Influenza H1N1 Imprinting Uncouples Serological and B-Cell Responses in Mice
papers.abstract: Antigenic drift reduces the protective potential of antibodies generated against earlier influenza variants. Unfortunately, a new infection or vaccination often preferentially recalls antibodies targeting previously encountered strains, thereby limiting responses to newly emerged variants. Although this phenomenon, known as immunological imprinting, has been well documented at the serological level, its underlying cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood. To resolve imprinting at both the serological and cellular level, we combined serum antibody profiling with targeted B-cell characterization in mice, including single-cell B-cell receptor (BCR) sequencing of germinal center (GC) B cells following secondary H1N1 challenge and bulk BCR sequencing of bone marrow plasma cells. We found that a primary infection with the 2009 pandemic H1N1 ("swine flu") strain largely prevented the generation of new serum antibodies following secondary exposure to the antigenically distinct H1N1 strain A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8), whereas the reciprocal infection sequence updated antibody specificities towards the last encountered virus. GC B cells did not mirror serological imprinting and instead generated updated BCR repertoires directed against the heterologous challenge strain. Likewise, BCR diversity in draining lymph node B cells failed to mirror the serological imprinting observed in the antibody response. Together, these findings reveal a striking uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, highlighting the need to study both compartments to better understand immune memory and guide the development of improved seasonal influenza vaccines across a diverse population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, addressing the limitations of previous serological studies that did not fully elucidate the underlying cellular mechanisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved mice, with a primary infection with the 2009 pandemic H1N1 strain followed by a secondary challenge with a different H1N1 strain, and vice versa, to investigate imprinting at both serological and cellular levels.
analysis.methods: Serum antibody profiling and single-cell B-cell receptor (BCR) sequencing of germinal center (GC) B cells and bulk BCR sequencing of bone marrow plasma cells were used to characterize the immune response in mice.
analysis.main_results: A primary infection with the 2009 pandemic H1N1 strain largely prevented the generation of new serum antibodies following secondary exposure to a different H1N1 strain, while GC B cells and BCR diversity in draining lymph node B cells did not mirror serological imprinting.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings revealed a striking uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, highlighting the need to study both compartments to better understand immune memory and guide vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings have implications for improving seasonal influenza vaccines by understanding the uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses, which can help in developing more effective vaccines across a diverse population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of mice, which may not fully represent human responses, and the focus on a specific H1N1 strain, limiting generalizability to other influenza strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study in mice investigated the uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, revealing that primary infection with the 2009 pandemic H1N1 strain prevented new serum antibody generation following secondary exposure to a different H1N1 strain. The findings highlight the need to study both compartments to better understand immune memory and improve vaccine development.

papers.abstract_zh: 抗原漂移 降低了针对早期流感变种产生的抗体的保护潜力。不幸的是,新的感染或 疫苗接种 通常会优先回忆起针对先前遇到的菌株的抗体,从而限制了对新出现的变体的反应。尽管这种被称为免疫印记的现象在血清学水平上已得到充分记录,但其潜在的细胞机制仍然知之甚少。为了解决血清学和细胞水平上的印记问题,我们将小鼠的血清抗体分析与靶向 B 细胞表征相结合,包括二次 H1N1 攻击后生发中心 (GC) B 细胞的单细胞 B 细胞受体 (BCR) 测序和骨髓浆细胞的批量 BCR 测序。我们发现,2009 年大流行的 H1N1(“猪流感”)毒株的初次感染在很大程度上阻止了继二次接触抗原独特的 H1N1 毒株 A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8) 后新血清抗体的产生,而相互感染序列更新了针对上次遇到的病毒的抗体特异性。GC B 细胞不反映血清学印记,而是生成针对异源攻击菌株的更新的 BCR 库。同样,引流淋巴结 B 细胞中的 BCR 多样性未能反映抗体反应中观察到的血清学印记。总之,这些发现揭示了流感印记过程中细胞和血清学 免疫应答 的惊人解偶联,强调需要研究这两个区室,以更好地了解免疫记忆并指导在不同人群中改进 季节性流感 疫苗 的开发。

papers.title: Genomic Surveillance and Evolution of Influenza Virus Across Two Consecutive Seasons, 2024–2026, in Southern Greece
papers.abstract: Continuous genomic surveillance of influenza virus is critical for monitoring viral evolution, detecting emerging variants, and informing vaccine strain selection. While partial-gene Sanger sequencing has traditionally underpinned national surveillance programs, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) enables simultaneous characterization of all eight genomic segments, providing resolution not achievable through conventional approaches. This is the first published, systematic, whole-genome-based influenza surveillance study reported from Greece. We sequenced and characterized influenza viruses circulating in Southern Greece (S. Greece) during two consecutive influenza seasons, 2024–2025 and 2025–2026, using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing. A total of 40 samples were analyzed, with complete or near-complete genome assembly achieved in the vast majority of them. During 2024–2025, co-circulation of A(H1N1)pdm09 (subclades C.1.9.3 and D.3.1), A(H3N2) (subclades J.1.1 and J.2.2), and B/Victoria (C.5 subclades, predominantly C.5.7) influenza viruses was confirmed, with the detection of an oseltamivir-resistant H1N1 variant carrying NA H275Y as a clinically significant finding. Extension of surveillance into 2025–2026 revealed a complete inter-seasonal lineage transition in A(H1N1)pdm09 from subclade C.1.9.3 to D.3.1/D.3.1.1, and the rapid emergence and geographic dissemination of A(H3N2) subclade K across multiple regions of Southern Greece. Phylogenetic analysis characterized the HA subclade composition across the two seasons and positioned the Greek strains within the European and global context. Sequences of subclade K strains from S. Greece were phylogenetically concordant with the updated 2026–2027 vaccine strains, in line with ECDC and WHO surveillance data. Whole-genome analysis confirmed the absence of virulence-associated polymerase markers in all isolates with fully assembled polymerase segments, and identified conserved internal segment substitution patterns co-segregating with circulating subclades. These findings provide the first published whole-genome evolutionary dataset for influenza in Southern Greece, contributing insight into subtype and clade-level evolutionary dynamics and demonstrating the public health value of sustained genomic surveillance at a national reference laboratory level.
