analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the genomic evolution of seasonal influenza viruses across two consecutive seasons in Southern Greece, emphasizing the importance of genomic surveillance for tracking viral evolution and informing vaccine strain selection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a systematic whole-genome-based influenza surveillance in Southern Greece during the 2024–2025 and 2025–2026 influenza seasons, analyzing a total of 40 samples with complete or near-complete genome assembly.
analysis.methods: The researchers used Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing to characterize influenza viruses circulating in Southern Greece during the two consecutive seasons, 2024–2025 and 2025–2026.
analysis.main_results: The study identified a complete inter-seasonal lineage transition in A(H1N1)pdm09 from subclade C.1.9.3 to D.3.1/D.3.1.1 and the rapid emergence and geographic dissemination of A(H3N2) subclade K across multiple regions of Southern Greece.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the dynamic evolutionary patterns of seasonal influenza viruses and demonstrate the value of sustained genomic surveillance in understanding subtype and clade-level changes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results contribute to the understanding of influenza evolution in Southern Greece and support the importance of genomic surveillance for vaccine strain selection and public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its relatively small sample size and focus on a specific geographic region, but the evidence is strong due to the use of whole-genome sequencing and alignment with international surveillance data.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted genomic surveillance of seasonal influenza viruses in Southern Greece during two consecutive seasons, 2024–2025 and 2025–2026, using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing. It identified a complete inter-seasonal lineage transition in A(H1N1)pdm09 from subclade C.1.9.3 to D.3.1/D.3.1.1 and the rapid emergence of A(H3N2) subclade K. The study also confirmed the absence of virulence-associated polymerase markers and identified conserved internal segment substitution patterns. These findings provide the first published whole-genome evolutionary dataset for influenza in Southern Greece, contributing to understanding subtype and clade-level dynamics and demonstrating the public health value of sustained genomic surveillance. The study's results align with ECDC and WHO surveillance data, supporting vaccine strain selection. However, the small sample size and regional focus limit the generalizability of the findings.

papers.abstract_zh: 流感病毒的连续 基因组监测 对于监测病毒 进化、检测新出现的变异并告知 疫苗 毒株选择至关重要。虽然部分基因桑格测序传统上是国家 监测 计划的基础,但全 基因组 测序 (WGS) 可以同时表征所有八个基因组片段,提供通过传统方法无法实现的分辨率。这是希腊报告的第一个发表的、系统的、基于整体 基因组 的流感 监测 研究。我们使用牛津纳米孔技术 (ONT) 测序技术对 2024-2025 年和 2025-2026 年连续两个流感季节在希腊南部 (S. Greek) 传播的流感病毒进行了测序和特征分析。总共分析了 40 个样品,其中绝大多数实现了完整或接近完整的 基因组 组装。2024-2025年期间,通过检测到携带NA的奥司他韦耐药H1N1变种,证实了甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09(亚进化枝C.1.9.3和D.3.1)、甲型H3N2流感病毒(亚进化枝J.1.1和J.2.2)和B/Victoria(C.5亚进化枝,主要是C.5.7)流感病毒的共同传播H275Y 是一项具有临床意义的发现。监测 延伸至 2025-2026 年揭示了 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 从分支 C.1.9.3 到 D.3.1/D.3.1.1 的完整季节间谱系转变,以及 甲型H3N2流感病毒 分支 K 在希腊南部多个地区的快速出现和地理传播。系统发育分析表征了两个季节的 HA 分支组成,并将希腊菌株定位在欧洲和全球背景下。来自希腊南部的 K 亚支菌株的序列在系统发育上与更新的 2026-2027 疫苗 菌株一致,与 ECDC 和 WHO 监测 数据一致。Whole-基因组 分析证实,在具有完全组装的聚合酶片段的所有分离株中不存在毒力相关聚合酶标记,并鉴定了与循环亚进化枝共分离的保守内部片段取代模式。这些发现提供了第一个发布的希腊南部流感的全 基因组 进化数据集,有助于深入了解亚型和分支水平的进化动态,并在国家参考实验室水平证明持续 基因组监测 的公共卫生价值。

papers.title: Genomic and Clinical Analysis of Influenza A in Hospitalized Adults, 2019-2024: Exploratory Evidence on Neuraminidase and Polymerase Acidic Protein Mutation-Outcome Associations From a Single Center.
papers.abstract: Background Antivirals are widely used to treat influenza, but potential resistance mutations remain a major challenge, and clinical data on key resistance mutations are limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 765 adults with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A admitted to Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, between 2019 and 2024 to determine whether specific NA/PA mutations are associated with severe outcomes or prolonged length of stay (LOS) when analyzed alongside key host factors. PA and NA sequences were obtained and linked to the clinical cohort for mutation-clinical outcome analyses. Multiple testing was addressed by controlling the false discovery rate using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results Among 765 inpatients with influenza A virus infection, the median age was 68 years; 5.0% were severe disease and 9.9% died. Older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, whereas antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Adjusted observational analyses showed a lower estimate for severe disease with baloxavir but no association with in-hospital death. Major high-level resistance mutations were absent; detected NA/PA mutations showed no robust association with severe disease or mortality. PA-F105L showed an exploratory association with longer LOS, but this finding was attenuated after adjustment and was confounded by clade and calendar period. Conclusions Clinical outcomes were driven mainly by host factors and admission severity. Detected NA/PA mutations were not robustly associated with severe outcomes, while high-level resistance could not be assessed; PA-F105L-LOS association requires phenotypic and external validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the association between specific neuraminidase (NA) and polymerase acidic (PA) mutations and clinical outcomes in hospitalized adults with influenza A virus infection. Conducted at Ruijin Hospital in Shanghai between 2019 and 2024, the study analyzed 765 patients with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A. The findings revealed that older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, while antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Although some mutations showed an exploratory association with prolonged length of stay, these findings were confounded by clade and calendar period. The study concluded that clinical outcomes were primarily driven by host factors and admission severity, and that the associations between NA/PA mutations and outcomes require further validation.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 抗病毒药物 被广泛用于治疗流感,但潜在耐药性 突变 仍然是一个重大挑战,并且关键耐药性 突变 的临床数据有限。方法 我们对 2019 年至 2024 年间上海瑞金医院收治的 765 名经 RT-PCR 确诊的甲型流感成人患者进行了回顾性 队列研究 研究,以确定在与关键 宿主 因素一起分析时,特定的 NA/PA 队列研究 是否与严重结局或住院时间延长 (LOS) 相关。获得 PA 和 NA 序列并将其与临床 队列研究 关联以进行 突变 临床结果分析。通过使用 Benjamini-Hochberg 程序控制错误发现率来解决多重测试问题。结果 765例甲型流感病毒感染住院患者中,中位年龄为68岁;5.0%为重症,9.9%死亡。年龄较大、较高的 CURB-65 评分和细菌/真菌合并感染是 死亡率 的主要相关因素,而 抗病毒药物 方案和 Ct 值与 死亡率 或严重结局不独立相关。调整后的观察分析显示,巴洛沙韦对严重疾病的估计较低,但与院内死亡无关。主要高层阻力位突变不存在;检测到的 NA/PA 突变 与严重疾病或 死亡率 没有显着相关性。PA-F105L 显示出与较长 LOS 的探索性关联,但这一发现在调整后减弱,并且受到进化枝和日历周期的混淆。结论 临床结果主要由 宿主 因素和入院严重程度决定。检测到的 NA/PA 突变 与严重后果没有显着相关性,同时无法评估高水平耐药性;PA-F105L-LOS 关联需要表型和外部验证。

papers.title: Earth-Abundant Kaolin Derived Antiviral Coating via Triple Synergistic Capture-Inactivate-Block Mechanism.
papers.abstract: Antiviral coating translation is constrained by additive aggregation and resin incompatibility. We upgrade natural kaolin into an efficient antiviral additive via thermal activation and one-pot ball milling with copper precursors, yielding amorphous metakaolin uniformly decorated with copper particles (Cu Ps). This solvent-free protocol suppresses Cu Ps agglomeration and ensures homogeneous dispersion within silicone-acrylic binders, essential for coating integrity. The metakaolin scaffold serves as a high-affinity viral capture platform, while anchored Cu Ps synergistically generate superoxide radicals (•O2-) and sustain localized Cu+/Cu2+ release, enabling dual-modal oxidative inactivation. Combined with the resin's physical barrier, this capture-oxidize-block mechanism delivers >99.9% inactivation of influenza A H3N2 and enterovirus EV-71 under ambient conditions. The composite supports kilogram-scale production (2.22 kg batch), maintains full activity after >6000 washing cycles, and passes dermal safety tests. This work transforms a low-cost clay mineral into a structurally engineered antiviral material and provides a scalable route that overcomes persistent manufacturability and durability limitations in surface protection.

papers.title: Population attributable mortality associated with respiratory viruses in Ontario, Canada: a population-based ecological analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory viruses are major contributors to population mortality, but cause-of-death coding undercounts their impact. Ecological regression models linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this limitation. Aim To estimate the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada (1993–2025), and to characterize temporal changes in virus-attributable mortality across the pandemic transition. Methods We analysed monthly all-cause mortality data with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fit for pre-pandemic (January 1993–February 2020) and combined pandemic (March 2020–February 2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions setting viral coefficients to zero. Sensitivity analyses examined temporal stratification of the pandemic period (Public Health Emergency of International Concern [PHEIC] period: March 2020–April 2023; post-PHEIC: May 2023–February 2025), exclusion of the early pandemic period (March–June 2020), and models without Fourier seasonal adjustment. Wald tests compared coefficients across specifications. Results Pre-pandemic, influenza A accounted for 1.8% (95% CI 1.4–2.3%) of mortality; influenza B showed no detectable impact. RSV demonstrated inverse associations in seasonally adjusted models but positive associations (PAF 1.9%, 95% CI 1.3–2.4%) without seasonal adjustment. Over the combined pandemic period (March 2020–February 2025; n=60 months), amid elevated baseline mortality (IRR 1.050, P=0.027), SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 6.1% (95% CI 4.2–8.0%) of deaths, approximately 4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden, despite widespread vaccination and antiviral availability. Model-estimated SARS-CoV-2-attributable deaths closely matched reported COVID-19 deaths from Public Health Ontario over the same period. Temporal stratification identified a significant increase in SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in the post-PHEIC period (PAF 9.8%, 95% CI 1.1–17.7%; p=0.027), while post-PHEIC influenza A and B attributable fractions did not differ significantly from pre-pandemic baselines. Excluding March-June 2020 yielded a conservative SARS-CoV-2 PAF of 5.7% (95% CI 3.3–8.1%), confirming robustness of primary estimates. Meta-analyses showed substantial heterogeneity for influenza A (I2=92.8%) and RSV (I2=89.1%) across modeling approaches, but minimal heterogeneity for SARS-CoV-2 (I2=5.5%). Conclusion SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3–4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures. Post-PHEIC data suggest that the burden of respiratory virus mortality, including for influenza, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels, highlighting the continued importance of respiratory virus prevention strategies. Estimates for influenza A and RSV were sensitive to seasonal adjustment, highlighting the importance of modelling choices when quantifying virus-attributable mortality.

Ecological regression models linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this limitation. Aim To estimate the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada (1993–2025), and to characterize temporal changes in virus-attributable mortality across the pandemic transition. Methods We analysed monthly all-cause mortality data with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fit for pre-pandemic (January 1993–February 2020) and combined pandemic (March 2020–February 2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions setting viral coefficients to zero. Sensitivity analyses examined temporal stratification of the pandemic period (Public Health Emergency of International Concern [PHEIC] period: March 2020–April 2023; post-PHEIC: May 2023–February 2025), exclusion of the early pandemic period (March–June 2020), and models without Fourier seasonal adjustment. Wald tests compared coefficients across specifications. Results Pre-pandemic, influenza A accounted for 1.8% (95% CI 1.4–2.3%) of mortality; influenza B showed no detectable impact. RSV demonstrated inverse associations in seasonally adjusted models but positive associations (PAF 1.9%, 95% CI 1.3–2.4%) without seasonal adjustment. Over the combined pandemic period (March 2020–February 2025; n=60 months), amid elevated baseline mortality (IRR 1.050, P=0.027), SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 6.1% (95% CI 4.2–8.0%) of deaths, approximately 4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden, despite widespread vaccination and antiviral availability. Model-estimated SARS-CoV-2-attributable deaths closely matched reported COVID-19 deaths from Public Health Ontario over the same period. Temporal stratification identified a significant increase in SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in the post-PHEIC period (PAF 9.8%, 95% CI 1.1–17.7%; p=0.027), while post-PHEIC influenza A and B attributable fractions did not differ significantly from pre-pandemic baselines. Excluding March-June 2020 yielded a conservative SARS-CoV-2 PAF of 5.7% (95% CI 3.3–8.1%), confirming robustness of primary estimates. Meta-analyses showed substantial heterogeneity for influenza A (I2=92.8%) and RSV (I2=89.1%) across modeling approaches, but minimal heterogeneity for SARS-CoV-2 (I2=5.5%). Conclusion SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3–4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures. Post-PHEIC data suggest that the burden of respiratory virus mortality, including for influenza, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels, highlighting the continued importance of respiratory virus prevention strategies. Estimates for influenza A and RSV were sensitive to seasonal adjustment, highlighting the importance of modelling choices when quantifying virus-attributable mortality.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道病毒是 死亡率 群体的主要贡献者,但死因编码低估了其影响。将病毒循环与 死亡率 波动联系起来的生态回归模型可以解决这一限制。目的 估计加拿大安大略省(1993-2025 年)与甲型和乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 死亡率 的人群归因分数 (PAF),并描述大流行过渡期间病毒归因 死亡率 的时间变化。方法 我们利用实验室 监测 指标分析了甲型、乙型、RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 流感的每月全因 死亡率 数据。具有长期趋势、傅里叶季节性项和人口偏移的负二项式模型适合大流行前(1993年1月至2020年2月)和大流行合并时期(2020年3月至2025年2月)。PAF 源自将病毒系数设置为零的反事实预测。敏感性分析检查了大流行期间的时间分层(国际关注的突发公共卫生事件 [PHEIC] 期间:2020 年 3 月至 2023 年 4 月;PHEIC 后:2023 年 5 月至 2025 年 2 月),排除了大流行早期(2020 年 3 月至 6 月),以及没有傅里叶季节调整的模型。Wald 测试比较了不同规格的系数。结果 大流行前,甲型流感占 死亡率 的 1.8%(95% CI 1.4–2.3%);乙型流感没有显示出可检测到的影响。RSV 在经季节性调整的模型中表现出负相关,但在未经季节调整的情况下呈正相关(PAF 1.9%,95% CI 1.3–2.4%)。在整个大流行期间(2020年3月至2025年2月;n=60个月),在基线死亡率升高(IRR 1.050,P=0.027)的情况下,SARS-CoV-2占死亡人数的6.1%(95% CI 4.2-8.0%),大约是大流行前甲型流感负担的4倍,尽管疫苗接种和抗病毒药物 可用性。模型估计的 SARS-CoV-2 死亡人数与同期安大略省公共卫生部门报告的 COVID-19 死亡人数非常吻合。时间分层发现,PHEIC 后时期 SARS-CoV-2 归因的 死亡率 显着增加(PAF 9.8%,95% CI 1.1-17.7%;p=0.027),而 PHEIC 后甲型和 B 型流感归因分数与大流行前的基线没有显着差异。排除 2020 年 3 月至 6 月,保守的 SARS-CoV-2 PAF 为 5.7%(95% CI 3.3-8.1%),证实了初步估计的稳健性。荟萃分析显示,不同建模方法中甲型流感 (I2=92.8%) 和 RSV (I2=89.1%) 存在显着异质性,但 SARS-CoV-2 异质性极小 (I2=5.5%)。结论 尽管有可用的对策,但 SARS-CoV-2 与 死亡率 人群负担比 季节性流感 A 高 3-4 倍相关。PHEIC 后的数据表明,呼吸道病毒 死亡率(包括流感病毒)的负担尚未恢复到大流行前的水平,这凸显了呼吸道病毒预防策略的持续重要性。甲型流感和 RSV 的估计对季节性调整敏感,突出了在量化病毒归因 死亡率 时建模选择的重要性。

papers.title: Air sampling for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural Zambia: a prospective comparison with human surveillance
papers.abstract: Respiratory infections are the leading cause of acute disease incidence globally and disproportionately burden low- and middle-income countries where surveillance capacity is limited. While facility-based surveillance remains the standard for respiratory pathogen monitoring in human populations, environmental air sampling offers potential advantages as a non-invasive supplementary method. We conducted a prospective environmental air sampling study nested within ongoing respiratory disease surveillance at Macha Hospital in Southern Province, Zambia, from July 2025 to June 2026. Air samplers were deployed continuously in the outpatient department and three inpatient wards, with filters collected and tested three times weekly. Surveillance in the patient population was conducted year-round with nasopharyngeal samples collected from patients with influenza-like illness. All samples were tested for influenza A/B virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 using the Cepheid GeneXpert platform. We analyzed concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples using percent agreement, Cohen's Kappa, Spearman correlations, and logistic regression with generalized estimating equations. Over 12 months, 596 air samples and 701 human samples were analyzed. Influenza A virus was the most common pathogen, detected in 38 air samples and 87 nasopharyngeal samples, with most cases detected from July to September 2025. For Influenza A, there was strong same-week concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (80.4% overall agreement; 44.4% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.5; Spearman's rho = 0.57). SARS-CoV-2 was also common, detected in 18 air samples and 16 nasopharyngeal samples, with cases detected sporadically throughout the year. For SARS-CoV-2, there was limited concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (68.6% agreement; 23.8% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.2; Spearman's rho = 0.2). Influenza B virus (1 air and 13 nasopharyngeal samples positive) and RSV (0 air and 4 nasopharyngeal samples positive) circulated sporadically, and unsurprisingly, gave limited concordance between samples. Cycle threshold values for influenza A virus (median for target 1: 36.7 vs. 25.1; p<0.001; median for target 2: 39.5 vs. 28.6; p<0.001) and SARS-CoV-2 (median: 41.3 vs. 27.5; p<0.001) were significantly higher for positive air samples than for nasopharyngeal samples. Implementation challenges were documented, including intermittent power outages and compromised electrical outlets causing sampler shutdowns, as well as study awareness issues that required sensitization activities for both facility staff and patients. Air sampling was feasible and demonstrated promise as a supplementary method for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural resource-limited settings. These findings support integrating environmental air sampling alongside surveillance in patient populations as part of a multimodal approach to respiratory pathogen monitoring.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究表明,空气采样可以与人类 监测 并行检测呼吸道病原体,根据病毒的不同,具有不同程度的一致性。这些发现支持将环境空气采样与 监测 结合到患者群体中,作为呼吸道病原体监测多模式方法的一部分。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,空气采样可能是农村资源有限环境中呼吸道病原体 监测 的一个有价值的工具,补充了传统的基于人类的方法。这可以提高 监测 系统在医疗基础设施有限的地区的及时性和覆盖范围。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 记录了实施挑战,包括间歇性断电和电源插座损坏导致采样器关闭,以及需要对设施工作人员和患者进行宣传活动的研究意识问题。由于这些后勤限制和潜在的抽样偏差,证据是中等的。

papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道感染是全球急性疾病的主要原因,给能力有限的低收入和中等收入国家带来不成比例的负担。虽然基于设施的 监测 仍然是人群呼吸道病原体监测的标准,但环境空气采样作为一种非侵入性补充方法具有潜在的优势。2025 年 7 月至 2026 年 6 月,我们在赞比亚南部省马查医院针对正在发生的呼吸道疾病 监测 进行了一项前瞻性环境空气采样研究。在门诊部和三个住院病房连续部署空气采样器,每周收集和测试 3 次过滤器。监测 全年在患者人群中进行,采集自流感样疾病患者的鼻咽样本。使用 Cepheid GeneXpert 平台对所有样本进行了甲型/乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 检测。我们使用一致性百分比、Cohen's Kappa、Spearman 相关性以及带有广义估计方程的逻辑回归来分析空气和鼻咽样本之间的一致性。12 个月内,分析了 596 个空气样本和 701 个人体样本。甲型流感病毒是最常见的病原体,在 38 个空气样本和 87 个鼻咽样本中检测到,大多数病例是在 2025 年 7 月至 9 月期间检测到的。对于甲型流感,空气样本和鼻咽样本之间存在很强的同周一致性(总体一致性为 80.4%;阳性一致性为 44.4%;Cohen's Kappa = 0.5;Spearman's rho = 0.57)。SARS-CoV-2 也很常见,在 18 个空气样本和 16 个鼻咽样本中检测到,全年都有零星病例发现。对于 SARS-CoV-2,空气样本和鼻咽样本之间的一致性有限(68.6% 一致;23.8% 阳性一致;Cohen's Kappa = 0.2;Spearman's rho = 0.2)。B 型流感病毒(1 个空气样本和 13 个鼻咽样本呈阳性)和 RSV(0 个空气样本和 4 个鼻咽样本呈阳性)零星传播,并且毫不奇怪,样本之间的一致性有限。阳性空气样本的甲型流感病毒循环阈值(目标 1 的中位数:36.7 vs. 25.1;p<0.001;目标 2 的中位数:39.5 vs. 28.6;p<0.001)和 SARS-CoV-2(中位数:41.3 vs. 27.5;p<0.001)显着高于鼻咽样本。记录了实施挑战,包括间歇性断电和电源插座损坏导致采样器关闭,以及需要对设施工作人员和患者进行宣传活动的研究意识问题。空气采样是可行的,并且被证明有望作为农村资源有限环境中基于设施的呼吸道病原体 监测 的补充方法。这些发现支持将环境空气采样与 监测 结合到患者群体中,作为呼吸道病原体监测多模式方法的一部分。

papers.title: The relationship between the oral health status and COVID-19 and Influenza infections
papers.abstract: Abstract A relationship has been reported between oral hygiene and influenza infection. Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and influenza are major respiratory virus infections. The oral cavity may act as both an entry site and reservoir for these viruses. The present study examined the role of oral health in SARS-CoV-2 infection through epidemiology and histopathology. A prospective observational study was also conducted to investigate whether good oral hygiene habits contribute to the prevention of respiratory viral infections. In the epidemiological study using data from health/dental check-ups and the Japanese National Health Insurance database, a multivariate analysis identified poor oral hygiene as an independent risk factor for the onset of COVID-19. A histopathological analysis revealed that the expression of the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor and furin in the gingival epithelium was higher with than without inflammation. The prospective observational study comparing two groups with different oral hygiene habits suggested that good oral hygiene practices with interdental brushes and mouthwash prevented the onset of COVID-19 and influenza. Collectively, these results indicate that poor oral hygiene contributes to the onset of COVID-19 infection by increasing ACE2 and furin expression. Furthermore, improvements in oral hygiene may prevent the onset of COVID-19 and influenza.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between oral health status and the onset of respiratory viral infections, including influenza.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 据报道,口腔卫生与流感感染之间存在关系。2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 和流感是主要的呼吸道病毒感染。口腔可能充当这些病毒的进入位点和 储存宿主。本研究通过 流行病学 和组织病理学研究了口腔健康在 SARS-CoV-2 感染中的作用。还进行了一项前瞻性观察研究,以调查良好的口腔卫生习惯是否有助于预防呼吸道病毒感染。在使用健康/牙科检查和日本国民健康保险数据库数据的流行病学研究中,多变量分析确定口腔卫生不良是 COVID-19 发病的独立危险因素。组织病理学分析显示,有炎症的牙龈上皮中血管紧张素转换酶 2 (ACE2) 受体和弗林蛋白酶的表达高于没有炎症的牙龈上皮。这项前瞻性观察性研究比较了两组具有不同口腔卫生习惯的人群,结果表明,使用牙间刷和漱口水等良好的口腔卫生习惯可以预防 COVID-19 和流感的发作。总的来说,这些结果表明,不良的口腔卫生会增加 ACE2 和弗林蛋白酶的表达,从而导致 COVID-19 感染的发生。此外,改善口腔卫生可以预防 COVID-19 和流感的发作。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查口腔健康状况与呼吸道病毒感染(包括流感)发病之间的关系。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 进行了一项前瞻性观察研究,比较具有不同口腔卫生习惯的个体,重点关注他们发生呼吸道病毒感染的风险。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究使用了健康和牙科检查的流行病学数据以及日本国民健康保险数据库,以及牙龈上皮的组织病理学分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 多变量分析确定口腔卫生不良是 COVID-19 发病的独立危险因素,组织病理学分析显示发炎的牙龈上皮中 ACE2 受体和弗林蛋白酶表达较高。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,不良的口腔卫生可能会通过改变受体表达来增加对呼吸道病毒感染的易感性,这为口腔健康在病毒感染中的作用提供了新的视角。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了保持口腔卫生作为预防呼吸道病毒感染(包括流感)的潜在预防措施的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,依赖于自我报告的数据,这可能会引入偏差。然而,这些证据得到了流行病学和组织病理学分析的支持,提供了中等程度的置信度。

papers.full_text: AbstractObjectiveTo evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults aged ≥18 years living with HIV and to provide evidence supporting influenza vaccination in this population in China.MethodsThis single-center, open-label comparative analysis was derived from a larger three-arm clinical study. For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2). Participants in both groups received one dose of IIV3 (0.5 mL) on Day 0. Blood samples were collected before and 28 days after vaccination for hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains. Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, geometric mean titer (GMT), and geometric mean increase (GMI). Safety was assessed by monitoring solicited and unsolicited adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up. An unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV from the original trial was included only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza-like illness (ILI), without assessment of vaccine efficacy.ResultsA total of 489 participants were enrolled, including 237 in Group 1 and 252 in Group 2. At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A(H1N1) (91.00% vs. 86.69%, P > 0.05), but significantly lower for A(H3N2) (49.50% vs. 89.52%) and B/Victoria (40.00% vs. 64.52%) (both P < 0.001). Seroprotection rates were also lower in Group 1 than in Group 2 for A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria (94.00% vs. 97.98%, 63.50% vs. 97.18%, and 40.50% vs. 68.55%, respectively). Post-vaccination GMTs were significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains (all P < 0.001). GMI was higher for A(H1N1) but lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Group 1 than in Group 2 (all P < 0.001). Multivariable analyses showed that HIV infection remained independently associated with several measures of vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, particularly for A(H3N2). IIV3 was generally safe and well tolerated. Most AEs were mild in severity, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine-related SAEs were reported. During the period from 29 days to 6 months after vaccination, few influenza-like illness events were reported among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV; these findings were descriptive and were not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza.ConclusionAdults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of response varied across influenza strains. A(H1N1) seroconversion was high in adults living with HIV, whereas responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower than those in HIV-uninfected adults. HIV infection remained associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses for several strain-specific outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with associations particularly evident for A(H3N2). IIV3 was safe and well tolerated, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV.Clinical trial registrationhttps://www.chictr.org.cn/showprojEN.html?proj=255613, identifier ChiCTR2500112191.Keywords: HIV infection, immunogenicity, safety, seroprotection, trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine MethodsStudy design and participantsThis study was a single-center, open-label comparative analysis derived from a larger three-arm clinical study conducted in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China, in which participants living with HIV were randomized to vaccination or no vaccination. Participant recruitment was conducted at Hangzhou Xixi Hospital of Hangzhou Medical College and three community health service centers in Xihu District, Hangzhou. Participants living with HIV and HIV-uninfected participants were enrolled concurrently during the same study period. The present analysis evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of IIV3 in adults living with HIV and compared vaccine-induced immune responses with those in an age- and sex-comparable group of HIV-uninfected adults.For the present comparative analysis, 472 vaccinated participants were planned, including 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2). Participants living with HIV were stratified by age (18–49 years and ≥50 years) and recruited primarily from the study hospital, whereas HIV-uninfected adults were recruited from both hospital- and community-based settings. Group 2 was selected to be age- and sex-comparable to Group 1 without individual matching. All participants included in the present analysis received a single 0.5 mL dose of IIV3 administered intramuscularly into the deltoid muscle on Day 0.Blood samples were collected before vaccination (Day 0) and 28 days after vaccination to assess HI antibody responses. Participants were provided with diary cards to record adverse events (AEs) following vaccination. Solicited and unsolicited AEs were monitored after vaccination, and serious adverse events (SAEs) were collected throughout the 6-month follow-up period.The original trial also included an unvaccinated cohort of adults living with HIV. Data from this cohort were used only for an exploratory, descriptive analysis of influenza-like illness (ILI) during follow-up. Because ILI was not virologically confirmed, this analysis was considered hypothesis-generating and was not intended to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza. At the time of study conduct, seasonal influenza vaccination in China was voluntary and outside the National Immunization Program. Chinese technical guidelines recommended annual influenza vaccination for all individuals aged ≥6 months without contraindications, with priority given to key and high-risk populations (9). The inclusion of the unvaccinated group of adults living with HIV was considered in this policy context, and randomization concerned receipt of the study influenza vaccine only without affecting routine HIV care or antiretroviral therapy. The parent study protocol was approved by the relevant ethics committees, and all participants provided written informed consent.Participants included in the present analysis were adults aged ≥18 years who had not received any influenza vaccine within the year preceding enrollment and had a body temperature <37.3 °C at enrollment. Female participants of childbearing potential were required to use effective contraception and have no pregnancy plans during the study period.Key exclusion criteria included a history of severe allergic reactions to influenza vaccines or vaccine components, pregnancy or breastfeeding, use of immunosuppressive agents within 1 month before enrollment, receipt of blood products or immunoglobulins within 3 months before enrollment, acute febrile illness, Guillain–Barré syndrome, coagulation disorders contraindicating intramuscular injection, or any condition that, in the investigator’s judgment, could interfere with study assessments.Study endpointsThe primary endpoint was the seroconversion rate against influenza A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains in Group 1 at 28 days after vaccination. Secondary endpoints included comparisons of seroconversion rates, seroprotection rates, GMTs, and GMIs between Group 1 and Group 2. Exploratory endpoints included evaluation of demographic and clinical factors associated with vaccine-induced immune responses. Additional analyses among participants living with HIV evaluated recent CD4+ T-cell count, time since HIV diagnosis, and duration of ART. Safety endpoints included AEs and SAEs following vaccination. ILI occurrence was also summarized descriptively as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating observation among vaccinated and unvaccinated participants living with HIV. ILI was defined as fever (≥38.0 °C) accompanied by cough or sore throat. ILI was identified based on clinical symptoms without virological confirmation and was therefore not used to assess vaccine efficacy against influenza.Sample size calculation and randomizationThis analysis was derived from a larger three-arm, single-center, open-label clinical study. The original sample size was calculated assuming seroconversion rates of 40% and 23% in vaccinated and unvaccinated adults living with HIV, respectively. With a two-sided α of 0.05, 95% power, and an anticipated dropout rate of 18%, 236 participants were required per group.In the original trial, participants living with HIV were stratified by age (18–49 years and ≥50 years) and randomly assigned to either the vaccinated or unvaccinated group using a stratified randomization sequence generated with SAS version 9.4 (SAS Institute, Cary, NC, USA). HIV-uninfected adults were enrolled separately as an age- and sex-comparable comparison group. For the present analysis, only vaccinated adults living with HIV and vaccinated HIV-uninfected adults were included.Study vaccineThe IIV3 (Shipulier®) was manufactured by Changchun Institute of Biological Products Co., Ltd. (Changchun, China). Each dose (0.5 mL per vial, batch number: TA20240725, expiration date: July 17, 2025) contained 15 μg of hemagglutinin antigen from each influenza virus strain included in the vaccine formulation. The IIV3 formulation corresponded to the WHO-recommended egg-based trivalent influenza vaccine composition for the 2024–2025 Northern Hemisphere season (10).Immunogenicity assessmentImmunogenicity was evaluated using the hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay performed at the Bioanalytical Center of Chongqing Meilaide Biopharmaceutical Co., Ltd. Serum HI antibody titers against influenza A(H1N1) (A/Victoria/4897/2022), A(H3N2) (A/Thailand/8/2022), and B/Victoria (B/Austria/1359417/2021) vaccine strains were measured before vaccination (Day 0) and 28 days after vaccination.Immunogenicity endpoints included seroconversion rate, seroprotection rate, GMTs, and GMIs. Seroconversion was defined as a pre-vaccination HI antibody titer <1:10 and a post-vaccination titer ≥1:40, or a pre-vaccination titer ≥1:10 with at least a four-fold increase after vaccination. Seroconversion rate was defined as the proportion of participants who achieved seroconversion. Seroprotection was defined as an HI antibody titer ≥1:40, and the seroprotection rate was defined as the proportion of participants achieving this threshold at the specified time point. GMTs were calculated for each influenza strain before and 28 days after vaccination. GMI was calculated as the geometric mean of the individual post-vaccination-to-pre-vaccination HI antibody titer ratios.Safety assessmentSafety assessments included all solicited and unsolicited AEs, regardless of their relationship to vaccination. Participants were observed for 30 minutes after vaccination and were provided with diary cards to record AEs occurring within 28 days after vaccination. Solicited local (injection-site pain, induration, swelling, rash, erythema, and pruritus) and systemic (fever, cough, headache, myalgia, arthralgia, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, and acute allergic reactions) AEs were collected during the first 7 days following vaccination. Any medical occurrence other than the predefined solicited events was recorded as an unsolicited AE through Day 28. SAEs were monitored for 6 months through active surveillance, consisting of scheduled on-site or telephone follow-up every 7 days, supplemented by spontaneous reporting from participants.Safety analyses compared the incidence, severity, and causality of AEs, as well as the incidence of SAEs, between Group 1 and Group 2. All reported AEs were graded for severity and assessed for causality by trained investigators according to the Guiding Principles for Grading Adverse Reactions in Clinical Trials of Preventive Vaccines (NMPA No. 102, 2019) (11).For participants living with HIV, planned hospitalizations or hospitalizations for routine clinical management that were scheduled before enrollment and did not reflect a worsening medical condition were not classified as SAEs, in accordance with the study protocol. All other events meeting the protocol-defined SAE criteria were reported and evaluated by the investigators.Statistical analysisStatistical analyses were performed using SAS version 9.4 (SAS Institute, Cary, NC, USA). GMTs, GMIs, and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated from log10-transformed HI antibody titers and back-transformed for presentation. Seroconversion and seroprotection rates were calculated with corresponding 95% CIs. Comparisons between groups were performed using the chi-square test, Fisher’s exact test, or t-test, as appropriate. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with seroconversion and seroprotection, whereas multivariable linear regression analyses were performed using individual-level log2-transformed post-vaccination HI antibody titers and log2-transformed antibody fold increases as continuous outcomes. Separate models were fitted for each influenza strain. Among vaccinated participants living with HIV and HIV-uninfected participants, models included age (18–49 vs. ≥50 years), sex, HIV infection status, comorbidity, and baseline log2 HI antibody titer. In exploratory analyses restricted to vaccinated participants living with HIV, models included age, sex, comorbidity, baseline log2 HI antibody titer, recent CD4+ T-cell count (<500 vs. ≥500 cells/μL), time since HIV diagnosis (<5 vs. ≥5 years), and duration of ART (<2 vs. ≥2 years). full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionSeasonal influenza remains an important cause of morbidity in adults living with HIV, and international guidelines recommend annual influenza vaccination for people living with HIV (6, 13). Previous systematic reviews have shown that influenza vaccines are generally safe and immunogenic in adults living with HIV, although immune responses vary across influenza strains and study populations (5, 14). More recently, a Chinese comparative study reported satisfactory antibody responses following quadrivalent influenza vaccination but lower immunogenicity among individuals with lower CD4+ T-cell counts (15). Our study extends these findings by providing contemporary evidence on the immunogenicity and safety of IIV3 in Chinese adults living with HIV and demonstrating strain-specific differences in vaccine-induced immune responses compared with HIV-uninfected adults.The most important finding of this study was the marked strain-specific variation in vaccine-induced immune responses. Although seroconversion against A(H1N1) was high in adults living with HIV and did not differ significantly between groups, antibody responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower in adults living with HIV than in HIV-uninfected adults. Similar findings have been reported previously, particularly for A(H3N2) (5, 15). These strain-specific differences may reflect a combination of host-, virus-, and exposure-related factors rather than HIV-associated immune dysfunction alone. Several mechanisms may contribute to the observed differences. Chronic HIV infection is associated with persistent immune activation and impaired B-cell and T follicular helper cell function, which may compromise high-quality antibody production despite effective ART (16, 17). In addition, A(H3N2) viruses undergo frequent antigenic drift, resulting in substantial antigenic diversity and contributing to the lower and more variable vaccine effectiveness observed for A(H3N2) than for other influenza subtypes (18, 19). Vaccine strain composition may also be relevant. Compared with the 2023–2024 Northern Hemisphere season, the A(H3N2) component of egg-based vaccines was updated from an A/Darwin/9/2021-like virus to an A/Thailand/8/2022-like virus for the 2024–2025 season, whereas the A(H1N1)pdm09 and B/Victoria components remained unchanged (10, 20). The recent update of the A(H3N2) vaccine component indicates that differences in prior antigenic exposure and pre-existing immunity may be relevant when interpreting the strain-specific responses. However, because both groups received the same vaccine and HI responses were assessed against homologous vaccine strains, antigenic drift alone is unlikely to explain the between-group differences. The unchanged B/Victoria component further suggests that recent vaccine-strain updating cannot account for all of the observed strain-specific variation. Accordingly, the comparatively lower responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria likely reflect multiple contributing factors, and the relative contribution of HIV-associated immune dysfunction cannot be determined from the present study. These strain-specific findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation across multiple influenza seasons and independent cohorts.The complementary global three-strain analysis provided an integrated assessment of humoral responses across the three vaccine strains. Although global response scores were lower in participants living with HIV at both Day 0 and Day 28, the Group × Time interaction was not statistically significant, indicating that the magnitude of increase from baseline did not differ significantly between groups in the primary global-response analysis. Notably, the lower global response observed in adults living with HIV at baseline persisted at Day 28, as confirmed by the model-based between-group contrast. In contrast, Tawfik et al. reported that the baseline difference between previously unvaccinated and vaccinated healthy adults was no longer significant by Day 90 (12), although direct comparison is limited by differences in study populations and assessment time points. Consistent with the global response findings, a substantially lower proportion of participants living with HIV achieved seroprotection against all three vaccine strains at Day 28. Together with the strain-specific analyses, the global three-strain assessment provides an integrated view of humoral immunity, showing that both groups mounted substantial antibody responses after vaccination, while between-group differences in the overall level and breadth of responses remained evident.Beyond the descriptive comparisons, multivariable analyses demonstrated that HIV infection remained independently associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for demographic characteristics, comorbidity, and baseline HI antibody levels. This finding indicates that the reduced immunogenicity observed in adults living with HIV was not fully accounted for by the measured baseline characteristics or baseline HI antibody levels. These findings support continued efforts to better understand and optimize influenza vaccine responses in people living with HIV, particularly for strains showing comparatively lower immunogenicity.In exploratory analyses restricted to participants living with HIV, recent CD4+ T-cell count, time since HIV diagnosis, and ART duration were not independently associated with vaccine-induced immune responses after adjustment for other covariates. Previous studies have reported inconsistent associations between these HIV-related factors and influenza vaccine immunogenicity, with lower CD4+ T-cell counts more consistently linked to reduced immune responses, whereas evidence regarding ART duration remains limited (5, 15). The absence of significant associations in our study may reflect the relatively preserved immune status and well-controlled HIV infection in this cohort, in which all participants were receiving ART and all participants with evaluable HIV RNA were virologically suppressed (<200 copies/mL). In contrast, baseline HI antibody level was consistently associated with post-vaccination immune responses, suggesting an important role of pre-existing influenza immunity in short-term vaccine responses. These exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger and more diverse cohorts.Baseline HI antibody level was consistently associated with vaccine-induced antibody responses in both the overall and HIV-restricted analyses. Higher baseline antibody levels were associated with greater odds of achieving seroprotection and higher post-vaccination antibody titers but smaller antibody increases after vaccination. This pattern has been consistently reported in influenza vaccine studies and likely reflects a ceiling effect, whereby individuals with higher pre-existing immunity have less potential for further fold increases despite achieving higher absolute antibody titers (21, 22). These findings highlight the importance of accounting for baseline HI antibody levels when evaluating vaccine immunogenicity and support their inclusion as a continuous covariate in multivariable analyses.Older age was associated with reduced immune responses to A(H3N2) but enhanced responses to B/Victoria. Although immunosenescence is known to influence influenza vaccine immunogenicity, age-related effects vary across influenza strains and study populations (23, 24). Although age was a prespecified stratification factor, the study was not specifically powered to detect age-related differences in vaccine-induced immune responses. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.Consistent with previous evidence, IIV3 was well tolerated in adults living with HIV, with no vaccine-related SAEs observed. full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionIn conclusion, adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of vaccine-induced immune responses varied across influenza strains. Compared with HIV-uninfected adults, adults living with HIV showed high seroconversion against A(H1N1), whereas immune responses to A(H3N2) and B/Victoria were generally lower. HIV infection remained independently associated with reduced vaccine-induced immune responses for several strain-specific outcomes after adjustment for demographic and clinical factors, although residual confounding from unmeasured factors cannot be excluded. Baseline HI antibody level was consistently associated with post-vaccination antibody responses. IIV3 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and was well tolerated in adults living with HIV. These findings provide contemporary evidence supporting annual influenza vaccination in adults living with HIV in China and highlight the importance of considering strain-specific differences when evaluating vaccine immunogenicity in this population. Further multicenter studies with longer follow-up are warranted to assess the durability of immune responses and their relationship with clinical protection.

papers.title_original: Immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine in adults living with HIV compared with HIV-uninfected adults: a study from China

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults living with HIV compared with HIV-uninfected adults, addressing the knowledge gap about how HIV affects vaccine responses in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a single-center, open-label comparative analysis derived from a larger three-arm clinical study conducted in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China. It included 236 adults living with HIV (Group 1) and 236 age- and sex-comparable HIV-uninfected adults (Group 2).
analysis.methods: Immunogenicity was assessed using hemagglutination inhibition (HI) antibody testing against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains, with blood samples collected before and 28 days after vaccination. Safety was evaluated by monitoring adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) during 6 months of follow-up.
analysis.main_results: At 28 days post-vaccination, seroconversion rates did not differ significantly between Group 1 and Group 2 for A(H1N1), but were significantly lower in Group 1 for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria (all P < 0.001). Post-vaccination GMTs were also significantly lower in Group 1 for all three strains. Most AEs were mild, and no Grade 4 adverse reactions or vaccine-related SAEs were reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses following IIV3 vaccination, although the magnitude of response varied across influenza strains, particularly for A(H3N2).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that IIV3 is safe and well tolerated in adults living with HIV, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in this population, and highlight the need for further research on strain-specific immune responses in HIV-positive individuals.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of clinical symptoms to identify influenza-like illness (ILI) without virological confirmation, which precludes assessing vaccine efficacy. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the analysis and the lack of virological confirmation for ILI.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (IIV3) in adults living with HIV compared to HIV-uninfected adults in China. The research aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding vaccine responses in HIV-positive individuals. A total of 489 participants were enrolled, with 237 in the HIV group and 252 in the uninfected group. Immunogenicity was measured using hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assays against A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B/Victoria strains, while safety was assessed through monitoring adverse events. Results showed that seroconversion rates for A(H1N1) were similar between groups, but significantly lower for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in the HIV group. Post-vaccination GMTs were also lower in the HIV group for all three strains. Most adverse events were mild, and no serious adverse events were reported. The authors concluded that adults living with HIV developed substantial antibody responses to IIV3, though the magnitude varied by strain. The study supports current vaccination recommendations for HIV-positive adults but has limitations due to the lack of virological confirmation for ILI, which affects the assessment of vaccine efficacy. The evidence is moderate in strength.

elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that IIV3 is safe and well tolerated in adults living with HIV, supporting current recommendations for influenza vaccination in this population, and highlight the need for further research on strain-specific immune responses in HIV-positive individuals.

papers.title: Complementing Biosafety Levels With Societal Safety Levels
papers.abstract: Biosafety level (BSL) classifications of biological agents have succeeded at minimizing occupational risk inside laboratories, but largely neglect the potential for onward transmission. As a result, many non-transmissible pathogens that could kill at most one individual per person exposed require greater containment than 1918 influenza, a virus that killed 50-100 million and might cause a new pandemic today. Laboratory workers are consenting professionals; the public is not. We recommend complementing BSLs with explicit thresholds for expected societal harm. Here we formalize Societal Safety Levels (SSLs) based on expected public fatalities per year, which we quantify from (i) estimated probability of laboratory release, (ii) likelihood of societal transmission, and (iii) consequence. SSLs would apply specifically to laboratory research with replication-competent potential pandemic pathogens, and would not restrict field surveillance, sequencing, or countermeasure development using non-replicating systems or pandemic-incapable agents. We find that applying the 0.1 expected deaths per facility-year standard common across multiple major-hazard industries to potential pandemic pathogen research would require marked safety improvements. Complementing BSLs with SSLs would establish enforceable accident-safety thresholds for pandemic-capable pathogens, bringing high-risk biological research into alignment with the quantitative safety standards that help other hazardous industries operate with public acceptance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Biosafety level (BSL) classifications of biological agents have succeeded at minimizing occupational risk inside laboratories, but largely neglect the potential for onward transmission. The study addresses the need for a framework that considers societal safety in addition to laboratory biosafety.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a conceptual and policy analysis proposing the use of Societal Safety Levels (SSLs) for laboratory research involving replication-competent potential pandemic pathogens. It does not involve empirical data collection or specific populations.
analysis.methods: SSLs are formalized based on expected public fatalities per year, calculated from (i) estimated probability of laboratory release, (ii) likelihood of societal transmission, and (iii) consequence. The methods focus on quantifying societal harm thresholds for pandemic-capable pathogens.
analysis.main_results: We find that applying the 0.1 expected deaths per facility-year standard common across multiple major-hazard industries to potential pandemic pathogen research would require marked safety improvements.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that complementing BSLs with SSLs would establish enforceable accident-safety thresholds for pandemic-capable pathogens, aligning high-risk biological research with quantitative safety standards used in other hazardous industries.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of a more comprehensive safety framework for pandemic-capable pathogens, enhancing public health preparedness and risk management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on conceptual analysis and does not involve empirical data collection, which limits the strength of the evidence. However, the proposed framework is grounded in existing safety standards and is considered to have moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study proposes the introduction of Societal Safety Levels (SSLs) to complement existing Biosafety Levels (BSLs) for laboratory research involving replication-competent potential pandemic pathogens. The authors argue that BSLs primarily focus on minimizing occupational risk but neglect the societal implications of pathogen release. They suggest that SSLs, based on expected public fatalities per year, could provide enforceable thresholds for accident safety, aligning high-risk biological research with quantitative safety standards used in other hazardous industries. The study highlights the need for marked safety improvements in pandemic-capable pathogen research, using a standard common across major-hazard industries. While the analysis is conceptual, it offers a novel approach to balancing laboratory safety with public health risk management. The proposed framework may inform future policy development and enhance public health preparedness.

papers.title_zh: 用社会安全水平补充生物安全水平
papers.source_body_en: Biosafety level (BSL) classifications of biological agents have succeeded at minimizing occupational risk inside laboratories, but largely neglect the potential for onward transmission. As a result, many non-transmissible pathogens that could kill at most one individual per person exposed require greater containment than 1918 influenza, a virus that killed 50-100 million and might cause a new pandemic today. Laboratory workers are consenting professionals; the public is not. We recommend complementing BSLs with explicit thresholds for expected societal harm. Here we formalize Societal Safety Levels (SSLs) based on expected public fatalities per year, which we quantify from (i) estimated probability of laboratory release, (ii) likelihood of societal transmission, and (iii) consequence. SSLs would apply specifically to laboratory research with replication-competent potential pandemic pathogens, and would not restrict field surveillance, sequencing, or countermeasure development using non-replicating systems or pandemic-incapable agents. We find that applying the 0.1 expected deaths per facility-year standard common across multiple major-hazard industries to potential pandemic pathogen research would require marked safety improvements. Complementing BSLs with SSLs would establish enforceable accident-safety thresholds for pandemic-capable pathogens, bringing high-risk biological research into alignment with the quantitative safety standards that help other hazardous industries operate with public acceptance.

papers.title: Defining influenza epidemic zones through temporal clustering of global surveillance data
papers.abstract: Introduction: Modeling when influenza epidemics typically occur can help countries optimize surveillance, time clinical and public health interventions, and reduce the burden of influenza. Methods: We used influenza virus detections reported during 2011-2024 by 180 countries to the Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System, excluding years impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2023). We analyzed data by calendar year (week 1-52) or shifted year (week 30-29) time windows, based on when most influenza detections occurred in each country. For countries with sufficient data, we computed generalized additive models (GAMs) of each country's weekly influenza-positive tests to smooth and impute time series distributions. From these GAMs, we calculated each country's weekly influenza burden. Country-specific time series were grouped using ensemble consensus k-means clustering, reducing the Euclidean distance between time series within clusters. We calculated cluster-specific GAMs to estimate average seasonal timing. Countries without sufficient data were assigned to a cluster based on population-weighted latitudinal distance to a cluster's mean latitude. Results: We identified five clusters, or epidemic zones, from 111 countries with sufficient data. The influenza burden in epidemic zones A and B was consistent with a northern hemisphere pattern, with most influenza detections occurring during November-May, while epidemic zones D and E were characterized by southern hemisphere-like seasonal timing, with most influenza burden occurring during June-November (D) and May-November (E). Epidemic zone C had most influenza burden occurring during September-March ; most countries assigned to this cluster were in the tropics. Conclusion: Epidemic zones may serve as a useful tool to strengthen and optimize influenza surveillance for global health decision-making (e.g., during vaccine strain composition discussions) and to guide country preparedness efforts for seasonal influenza epidemics, including timing enhanced surveillance and informing the availability of prevention and control efforts.

papers.title_zh: 通过全球 监测 数据的时间聚类定义流感流行区
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Modeling when influenza epidemics typically occur can help countries optimize surveillance, time clinical and public health interventions, and reduce the burden of influenza. Methods: We used influenza virus detections reported during 2011-2024 by 180 countries to the Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System, excluding years impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2023). We analyzed data by calendar year (week 1-52) or shifted year (week 30-29) time windows, based on when most influenza detections occurred in each country. For countries with sufficient data, we computed generalized additive models (GAMs) of each country's weekly influenza-positive tests to smooth and impute time series distributions. From these GAMs, we calculated each country's weekly influenza burden. Country-specific time series were grouped using ensemble consensus k-means clustering, reducing the Euclidean distance between time series within clusters. We calculated cluster-specific GAMs to estimate average seasonal timing. Countries without sufficient data were assigned to a cluster based on population-weighted latitudinal distance to a cluster's mean latitude. Results: We identified five clusters, or epidemic zones, from 111 countries with sufficient data. The influenza burden in epidemic zones A and B was consistent with a northern hemisphere pattern, with most influenza detections occurring during November-May, while epidemic zones D and E were characterized by southern hemisphere-like seasonal timing, with most influenza burden occurring during June-November (D) and May-November (E). Epidemic zone C had most influenza burden occurring during September-March ; most countries assigned to this cluster were in the tropics. Conclusion: Epidemic zones may serve as a useful tool to strengthen and optimize influenza surveillance for global health decision-making (e.g., during vaccine strain composition discussions) and to guide country preparedness efforts for seasonal influenza epidemics, including timing enhanced surveillance and informing the availability of prevention and control efforts.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:对流感流行通常发生的时间进行建模可以帮助各国优化 监测、安排临床和公共卫生干预措施并减轻流感负担。方法:我们使用了 2011-2024 年期间 180 个国家向全球流感 监测 和响应系统报告的流感病毒检测结果,不包括受 COVID-19 大流行影响的年份(2020-2023 年)。我们根据每个国家大多数流感检测发生的时间,按日历年(第 1-52 周)或轮班年(第 30-29 周)时间窗口分析数据。对于拥有足够数据的国家,我们计算了每个国家每周流感阳性检测的广义加性模型(GAM),以平滑和估算时间序列分布。根据这些 GAM,我们计算了每个国家每周的流感负担。使用集成共识 k 均值聚类对特定国家/地区的时间序列进行分组,从而减少聚类内时间序列之间的欧几里得距离。我们计算了特定于集群的 GAM 来估计平均季节性时间。没有足够数据的国家根据人口加权纬度与聚类平均纬度的距离分配到一个聚类。结果:我们在数据充足的 111 个国家中确定了 5 个集群或流行区。A区和B区的流感负担与北半球模式一致,大部分流感检测发生在11月至5月;而D区和E区则具有类似南半球的季节性时间特征,大部分流感负担发生在6月至11月(D)和5月至11月(E)。C区流感负担主要发生在9月-3月;大多数分配到该组的国家都位于热带地区。结论:流行区可以作为加强和优化流感 监测 的有用工具,以促进全球卫生决策(例如,在 疫苗 毒株组成讨论期间),并指导各国针对 季节性流感 流行病的准备工作,包括加强 监测 的时间安排和通报预防和控制工作的可用性。

papers.title: Comparative immunogenicity of several inactivated influenza vaccines among healthcare workers in Hong Kong
papers.abstract: We compared the immunogenicity of three licensed egg-based inactivated influenza vaccines, including TetrAnflu (Sinovac quadrivalent), Fluarix Tetra (GSK quadrivalent), and Vaxigrip (Sanofi trivalent), in adult healthcare workers in Hong Kong during the 2025/26 season. Age- and sex-matched recipients (n=30-40 per group) with paired pre- and post-vaccination sera were identified from an ongoing cohort. Hemagglutination-inhibition assays were performed against the egg-propagated 2025/26 vaccine reference strains. The three vaccines induced broadly comparable geometric mean fold-rises, post-vaccination geometric mean titers, proportions achieving titers >=40, and seroconversion rates against vaccine strains. These real-world data support the interchangeability of the three products for seasonal influenza vaccination programs among healthcare workers.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the immunogenicity of three egg-based inactivated influenza vaccines—TetrAnflu, Fluarix Tetra, and Vaxigrip—among healthcare workers in Hong Kong during the 2025/26 season. The research aimed to address the need for understanding vaccine effectiveness in this population. Age- and sex-matched recipients with paired pre- and post-vaccination sera were identified from an ongoing cohort. Hemagglutination-inhibition assays were conducted against the egg-propagated 2025/26 vaccine reference strains. The results showed that all three vaccines induced comparable geometric mean fold-rises, post-vaccination geometric mean titers, proportions achieving titers >=40, and seroconversion rates against vaccine strains. These findings support the interchangeability of the vaccines in seasonal influenza vaccination programs for healthcare workers. The study provides relevant data for vaccine selection and use in this group. However, the evidence is based on a single cohort, which may limit generalizability.
